II. pl. εὐναί, stones used as anchors in the times of Hom. and Hes., and thrown out from the prow, while the stern was made fast to land, ἐκ δ’ εὐνὰς ἔβαλον κατὰ δὲ πρυμνήσι’ ἔδησαν Hom.

ευνηθεν.def: εὐνῆθεν (from εὐνή) from or out of bed, Od.

ευνητηρ.def: εὐνητήρ (εὐνάω) a bedfellow, husband, Aesch.:—doric fem. εὐνάτειρα, θεοῦ μὲν εὐν. partner of his bed, id.; εὐν. Διὸς λεχέων id.

ευνισ.def: εὖνις reft of, bereaved of, c. gen., Hom., Aesch.:—absol. bereaved of children, id. (deriv. uncertain)
εὖνις, ιδος (= εὐνέτις) a bedfellow, wife, Soph., Eur.

ευννητοσ.def: ἐΰν-νητος, ον (epic for εὔνητος) (νέω) well-spun, Hom.

ευνοεω.def: εὐνοέω (εὔνοος) to be well-inclined, Hdt., attic

ευνοια.def: εὔνοια, ης, ἡ, (εὔνους) I. good-will, favour, kindness, κατ’ εὔνοιαν out of kindness or good-will, Hdt.; δι’ εὐνοίας Thuc.; δι’ εὔνοιαν Plat.; εὐνοίας ἕνεκα Dem.; μετ’ or ὑπ’ εὐνοίας id.; ἐπ’ εὐνοίᾳ χθονός for love of fatherland, Aesch.; εὔνοιαν ἔχειν εἴς τινα ap. Dem.:—in pl. feelings of kindness, favours, Aesch. II. a gift in token of good-will, esp. of presents to the Athenian commanders from the subject states, Dem.

ευνοικοσ.def: εὐνοϊκός, ή, όν (from εὔνοια) well-disposed, kindly, favourable, Dem.: —adv., εὐνοϊκῶς ἔχειν τινί or πρός τινα to be kindly disposed to.., Xen.

ευνομεομαι.gloss: to have good laws, to be orderly
ευνομεομαι.def: εὐνομέομαι, Dep.:— to have good laws, to be orderly, Hdt., Thuc., etc.

ευνομια.def: εὐνομία, ἡ, 1. good order, order, Od., Hdt., attic 2. personified by Hes. as daughter of Themis.

ευνομοσ.def: εὔ-νομος, ον under good laws, well-ordered, Pind., Plat.

ευνουσ.def: εὔ-νους, ουν well-minded, well-disposed, kindly, friendly, Hdt., attic; τινι to one, Hdt., etc.; οἱ ἐμοὶ εὖνοι my well-wishers, Xen.; τὸ εὔνουν εὔνοια, Soph., etc.—comp. εὐνούστερος id., ionic εὐνοέστερος Hdt.; Sup. εὐνούστατος Ar.

ευνουχοσ.def: εὐν-οῦχος, ὁ, a eunuch, employed to take charge of the women and act as chamberlains (whence the name, οἱ τὴν εὐνὴν ἔχοντες), Hdt., Ar., etc.

ευνωμασ.def: εὐ-νώμας, ου, (νωμάω) moving well or regularly, εὐνώμᾳ χρόνῳ by the steady march of time, Soph.

ευξαντοσ.def: εὔ-ξαντος, ον (ξαίνω) well-carded, of wool, Anth.

ευξενοσ.def: εὔξενος I. kind to strangers, hospitable, ἀνδρῶνας εὐξένους δόμων the guest- chambers, Aesch.; λιμὴν εὐξεινότατος ναύταις Eur. II. πόντος εὔξεινος the Euxine, now the Black sea, Hdt., etc.:—anciently called ἄξενος, the inhospitable (dictus ab antiquis Axenus ille fuit, Ovid.).

ευξεστοσ.def: εὔξεστος (ξέω) well-planed, well-polished, of carpenters' work, Hom.

ευξοοσ.def: εὔξοος (ξέω) just like εὔξεστος, often in Hom.; σκέπαρνον ἐΰξοον an axe with polished haft, Od.

ευοδεω.def: εὐοδέω, (εὔοδος) to have a free course or passage, of running water, Dem.

ευοδια.gloss: a good journey, wishes for a good journey
ευοδια.def: εὐοδία, ἡ, (εὔοδος) a good journey, wishes for a good journey, Aesch. ap. Ar.

ευοδοσ.def: εὔ-οδος, ον easy to pass, of mountains, Xen.; of a road, easy to travel, id.

ευοδοω.def: εὐ-οδόω, 1. to help on the way, c. dat. pers., Soph. 2. Pass. to have a prosperous journey, NTest.:—metaph. to prosper, be successful, Hdt., NTest.

ευοι.def: εὐοῖ Bacchanalian exclamation, Lat. evoe, Soph., etc.

ευοινοσ.def: εὔ-οινος, ον producing good wine, Anth.

ευομολογητοσ.def: εὐ-ομολόγητος, ον easy to concede, indisputable, Plat.

ευοπλεω.def: εὐοπλέω, to be well-equipt, Anth. (from εὔοπλος)

ευοπλια.gloss: a good state of arms and equipments
ευοπλια.def: εὐοπλία, ἡ, (from εὔοπλος) a good state of arms and equipments, Xen.

ευοπλοσ.def: εὔ-οπλος, ον (ὅπλον) well-armed, well-equipt, Ar., Xen.

ευοργησια.def: εὐοργησία, ἡ, gentleness of temper, Eur. (from εὐόργητος)

ευοργητοσ.def: εὐ-όργητος, ον (ὀργή) good-tempered:—adv. -τως, with good temper, Thuc.

ευορκεω.gloss: to be faithful to one's oath
ευορκεω.def: εὐορκέω, to be faithful to one's oath, Eur., Thuc.

ευορκια.def: εὐορκία, ἡ, fidelity to one's oath, Pind. (from εὔορκος)

ευορκοσ.gloss: keeping one's oath, faithful to one's oath
ευορκοσ.def: εὔ-ορκος, ον I. keeping one's oath, faithful to one's oath, Hes., attic II. of oaths, εὔορκα ὀμνύναι to swear faithfully, attic; εὔορκόν [ἐστι] it is in accordance with one's oath, no breach of oath, Thuc.; εὔορκα ταῦθ’ ὑμῖν ἐστι Dem.; so in adv., τάδ’ εὐόρκως ἔχει Aesch.

ευορκωμα.def: εὐ-όρκωμα, ατος, τό, a faithful oath, Aesch.

ευορμοσ.def: εὔ-ορμος, ον 1. with good mooring-places, Hom., Soph. 2. well-moored, of ships, Anth.

ευορνισ.def: εὔ-ορνις, ῑθος, ὁ, ἡ, abounding in birds, Anth.

ευοφθαλμοσ.def: εὐ-όφθαλμος, ον with beautiful eyes, Xen.: keen-eyes, id.

ευοχθεω.def: εὐοχθέω, to be in good case, Hes. (from εὔοχθος)

ευοχθοσ.def: εὔ-οχθος, ον with goodly banks, fertile, epic Hom.:— generally abundant, rich, Eur.

ευπαγησ.def: εὐ-πᾰγής, ές (πήγνυμι) of the body, compact, firm, strong, Xen., Theocr.

ευπαθεια.gloss: the enjoyment of good things, comfort, ease
ευπαθεια.def: εὐπάθεια (from εὐπαθής) the enjoyment of good things, comfort, ease, Xen.:—esp. in pl. enjoyments, luxuries, ἐν εὐπαθίῃσι εἶναι to enjoy oneself, Hdt.; also delicacies, dainties, Xen.

ευπαθεω.gloss: to be well off, enjoy oneself, make merry
ευπαθεω.def: εὐπᾰθέω, to be well off, enjoy oneself, make merry, Hdt., Plat. (from εὐπᾰθής)

ευπαθησ.def: εὐ-πᾰθής, ές (πάσχω) I. enjoying good things, easy. II. easily affected, Plut.

ευπαιδια.def: εὐπαιδία, ἡ, a goodly race of children, Eur.; εὐπαιδίαν ἔχων blest in his children, id. (from εὔπαις)

ευπαισ.def: εὔ-παις, παιδος, ὁ, ἡ, blest in one's children, i. e. with many or good children, Hhymn., Hdt., attic; γόνος εὔπαις noble offspring, Eur.

ευπαλαμοσ.def: εὐ-πάλᾰμος, ον (παλάμη) handy, skilful, ingenious, inventive, Aesch., Anth.

ευπαραγωγοσ.def: εὐ-παράγωγος, ον (παράγω) easy to lead astray, Ar.

ευπαρακολουθητοσ.def: εὐ-παρᾰκολούθητος, ον (παρακολουθέω) easy to follow, of an argument, Arist.

ευπαρακομιστοσ.def: εὐ-παρακόμιστος, ον (παρακομίζω) easy to convey, Plut.

ευπαραοσ.def: εὐ-πάρᾱος, ον (doric for εὐπάρειος) (παρειά) with beauteous cheeks, Pind.

ευπαραπειστοσ.def: εὐ-παράπειστος, ον easily led away, Xen.

ευπαρεδροσ.def: εὐ-πάρεδρος, ον constantly attending, τὸ εὐπ. τῷ Κυρίῳ constant waiting on the Lord, NTest.

ευπαρυφοσ.def: εὐ-πάρῠφος, ον (παρυφή) 1. with fine purple border, Plut. 2. of persons, wearing such a garment, Lat. praetextatus, a grandee, Luc.

ευπατερεια.def: εὐ-πᾰτέρεια, ἡ, (πατήρ) 1. daughter of a noble sire, Hom. 2. of places, of a noble father, Eur.

ευπατριδησ.def: εὐ-πᾰτρίδης, ου, (πατήρ) I. of good or noble sire, of noble family, of persons, Soph., Eur., etc.; εὐπατρίδαι οἶκοι Eur. II. at Athens in the old time, the εὐπατρίδαι formed the first class (the Nobles), the γεωμόροι the second, the δημιουργοί the third, Xen. 2. at Rome, the Patricians, id.

ευπατρισ.def: εὔπᾰτρις, ιδος (πατήρ) born of a noble sire, Eur.; τίς ἂν εὔπατρις ὧδε βλάστοι; who could be born so worthy of a noble sire? Soph.; ἐλπίδων εὐπατρίδων of hopes derived from those of noble birth, id.

ευπατωρ.def: εὐ-πᾰ́τωρ, ορος, (πατήρ) born of a noble sire, Aesch.

ευπειθησ.def: εὐ-πειθής, ές (πείθω) I. ready to obey, obedient, τινι Aesch., Plat.; also τινος, id. II. act. persuasive, Aesch.

ευπεμπελοσ.def: εὐ-πέμπελος, ον a word of uncertain meaning in Aesch., either tranquil, placable, as if it were εὐπέμφελον (cf. δυσπέμφελος), or easy to be sent away (cf. δύσπεμπτος).

ευπενθεροσ.def: εὐ-πένθερος, ον with a good father-in-law, Theocr.

ευπεπτοσ.def: εὔ-πεπτος, ον (πέσσω) easy of digestion, Arist.

ευπεριαγωγοσ.def: εὐ-περιάγωγος, ον (περιάγω) easily turned round, Luc.

ευπεριγραφοσ.gloss: easy to sketch out, with a good outline
ευπεριγραφοσ.def: εὐ-περίγρᾰφος, ον (περιγράφω) easy to sketch out, with a good outline, Luc.

ευπερισπαστοσ.def: εὐ-περίσπαστος, ον (περισπάω) easy to pull away, Xen.

ευπεταλοσ.def: εὐ-πέτᾰλος, ον (πέταλον) with beautiful leaves, Anth.

ευπετεια.def: εὐπέτεια, ἡ, 1. ease, δι’ εὐπετείας easily, Eur.:—pl., εὐπετείας διδόναι to give facilities, Plat. 2. easiness of getting or having a thing, c. gen., Hdt., Xen. (from εὐπετής)

ευπετησ.def: εὐ-πετής, ές (πίπτω) I. of the dice, falling well; metaph. favourable, Aesch.; so in adv., εὐπετῶς ἔχειν id. 2. easy, without trouble, Lat. facilis, Hdt., attic:—adv. εὐπετῶς, ionic -έως, easily, Hdt., attic; with numerals, ἑξακοσίους ἀμφορέας εὐπ. χωρέει it easily holds 600 amphorae, i. e. full 600, Hdt.:—comp. -εστέρως id. II. of persons, easy-tempered, accommodating, Eur.

ευπετροσ.def: εὔ-πετρος, ον of good hard stone, Anth.

ευπηγησ.def: εὐ-πηγής, ές (= εὐπαγής,) well-built, stout, Od.

ευπηνοσ.def: εὔ-πηνος, ον (πήνη) of fine texture, Eur.

ευπιδαξ.def: εὐ-πῖδαξ, ακος, abounding in fountains, Anth.

ευπιστοσ.def: εὔ-πιστος, ον I. trustworthy, trusty, Xen.; εὔπιστα things easy to believe, Soph. II. act. easily believing, credulous, Arist.

ευπιων.def: εὐ-πῑ́ων, ονος, very fat: very rich, Anth.

ευπλατησ.def: εὐ-πλᾰτής, ές (πλάτος) of a good breadth, Xen.

ευπλειοσ.def: ἐΰ-πλειος, η, ον well filled, Od.

ευπλεκτοσ.def: εὔπλεκτος (πλέκω) well-plaited, well-twisted, of wicker-work and ropes, Il.; of nets, Eur.

ευπλοια.def: εὔπλοια (εὔπλοος) a fair voyage, Il., Soph.

ευπλοκαμοσ.def: εὐπλόκαμος with goodly locks, fairhaired, Hom.; εὐπλ. κόμαι goodly tresses, Eur.

ευπλουσ.def: εὔ-πλους, ουν (πλέω) good for sailing, εὔπλοον ὅρμον ἵκοιτο may he reach a friendly port, Theocr.

ευπλωτοσ.def: εὔ-πλωτος, ον favourable to sailing, Anth.

ευπνοια.def: εὔπνοια 1. easiness of breathing. 2. fragrance, Anth. (from εὔπνους)

ευπνουσ.gloss: breathing well, breathing a sweet smell, sweet-smelling
ευπνουσ.def: εὔπνους (πνέω) I. breathing well, breathing a sweet smell, sweet-smelling, Mosch., Anth. II. affording a free passage to the air, Lat. perflabilis, Xen.

ευποδια.def: εὐποδία, ἡ, (εὔπους) goodness of foot, Xen.

ευποιητοσ.def: εὐ-ποίητος, ον well-made, well-wrought, Od., Hes.

ευποικιλοσ.def: εὐ-ποίκῐλος, ον much varied, variegated, Anth.

ευποκοσ.def: εὔ-ποκος, ον rich in wool, fleecy, Aesch.

ευπολεμοσ.gloss: good at war, successful in war
ευπολεμοσ.def: εὐ-πόλεμος, ον good at war, successful in war, Hhymn., Xen.

ευπομποσ.def: εὔ-πομπος, ον conducting to a happy issue, Aesch., Soph.

ευπορεω.gloss: to prosper, thrive, be well off
ευπορεω.def: εὐπορέω, (εὔπορος) I. to prosper, thrive, be well off, Xen.; ὅθεν ὁ πόλεμος εὐπορεῖ from which sources war is successfully maintained, Thuc. b. c. gen. rei, to have plenty of, to have store of, to abound in a thing, c. gen., Xen., etc. 2. to find a way, find means, Thuc.: c. inf. to be able to do, Plat. II. c. acc. rei, to supply, furnish, Thuc., Dem., etc.

ευπορια.def: εὐπορία, ἡ, (εὔπορος) I. an easy way of doing a thing, facility or faculty for doing, c. inf., Thuc.; absol., Xen.:—c. gen. rei, easy means of providing, Thuc., etc. 2. plenty, store, abundance, wealth, Xen.:— in pl. advantages, Isocr., Dem. II. the solution of doubts or difficulties, Xen., etc.

ευποριστοσ.def: εὐ-πόριστος, ον (πορίζω) easy to procure;— εὐπόριστα (sc. φάρμακα) τά, common medicines, Plut.

ευποροσ.def: εὔ-πορος, ον I. easy to pass or travel through, Aesch.; τὰ εὔπορα open ground, Xen.; εὔπορόν ἐστι διϊέναι Thuc. 2. easily gotten, easily done, easy, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:— τὸ εὔπορον εὐπορία, id.; εὔπορόν ἐστι it is easy, c. inf., id. II. going easily, ready, glib, γλῶττα Ar. 2. of persons, full of resources or devices, ingenious, inventive, ready, opp. to ἄπορος, Ar., Plat. III. εὔπ. τινι well-provided with, rich in a thing, Thuc.:—absol. well off, wealthy, Dem. IV. adv. -ρως, easily, Xen.; comp. -ώτερον, Plat. 2. in abundance, εὐπ. ἔχειν πάντα Thuc.

ευποτμεω.def: εὐποτμέω, (from εὔποτμος) to be lucky, fortunate, Plut.

ευποτμια.def: εὐποτμία, ἡ, good fortune, Plut., Luc. (from εὔποτμος)

ευποτοσ.gloss: easy to drink, pleasant to the taste
ευποτοσ.def: εὔ-ποτος, ον easy to drink, pleasant to the taste, Aesch.

ευπουσ.def: εὔπους I. with good feet, Xen. II. of verses, with good feet, flowing, Anth.

ευπραγεω.gloss: to do well, be well off, flourish
ευπραγεω.def: εὐπρᾱγέω, (= εὖ πράσσω,) to do well, be well off, flourish, Thuc., Xen., etc.

ευπραγια.def: εὐπρᾱγία, ἡ, (from εὐπρᾱγέω) (= εὐπραξία,) well-doing, well-being, welfare, success, Thuc., etc.

ευπρακτοσ.def: εὔ-πρακτος, ον easy to be done, Xen.

ευπραξια.def: εὐπραξία I. = εὐπραγία, Hdt., Trag. II. good conduct, Xen.

ευπρεμνοσ.def: εὔ-πρεμνος, ον (πρέμνον) with good stem, Anth.

ευπρεπεια.def: εὐπρέπεια, ἡ, I. goodly appearance, dignity, comeliness, Thuc. II. colourable appearance, speciousness, plausibility, id., Plat. (from εὐπρεπής)

ευπρεπησ.def: εὐ-πρεπής, ές (πρέπω) I. well-looking, goodly, comely, of outward appearance, Hdt., attic; εὐπρ. ἰδεῖν fair to look on, Xen.; εἶδος εὐπρεπής Eur. 2. decent, seemly, fitting, becoming, Hdt., Aesch., Eur.; τελευτὴ εὐπρεπεστάτη a most glorious end, Thuc. 3. specious, plausible, Hdt., Thuc.; ἐκ τοῦ εὐπρεποῦς in pretence, id. II. adv. -πῶς, ionic πέως, Hdt., Aesch., etc.; comp. -πέστερον, Eur.; Sup. -πέστατα, Thuc.

ευπροσηγοροσ.def: εὐ-προσήγορος, ον easy of address, i. e. affable, courteous, Eur.; οὐκ εὐπρ. ἆται miseries that forbid my being spoken to, id.

ευπροσιτοσ.def: εὐ-πρόσῐτος, ον easy of access, of places, Luc.

ευπροσοδοσ.def: εὐ-πρόσοδος, ον 1. of persons, accessible, affable, Lat. qui faciles aditus habet, Thuc., Xen. 2. of places, easily accessible, id.

ευπροσοιστοσ.def: εὐ-πρόσοιστος, ον easy of approach: generally, easy, Eur.

ευπροσωπεω.def: εὐπροσωπέω, to make a fair show, NTest.

ευπροσωποκοιτησ.gloss: lying so as to present a fair face
ευπροσωποκοιτησ.def: εὐπροσωπο-κοίτης, ου, (κοίτη) lying so as to present a fair face, Aesch.

ευπροσωποσ.def: εὐ-πρόσωπος, ον (πρόσωπον) 1. fair of face, Ar., Xen.: with glad countenance, Soph. 2. metaph. fair in outward show, specious, Hdt., Eur., etc.

ευπροφασιστοσ.def: εὐ-προφάσιστος, ον with good pretext, plausible, Thuc.

ευπρυμνοσ.def: εὔ-πρυμνος, ον (πρύμνα) with goodly stern, Il., Eur.

ευπρωροσ.def: εὔ-πρῳρος, ον (πρῷρα) with goodly prow, Eur.

ευπτεροσ.def: εὔ-πτερος, ον (πτερόν) well-winged, well-plumed, Soph., Eur.; metaph., of high-plumed dames, Ar.

ευπτερυγοσ.def: εὐ-πτέρῠγος, ον (πτέρυξ) (= εὔπτερος, of ships, Anth.)

ευπτορθοσ.def: εὔ-πτορθος, ον finely branching, of horns, Anth.

ευπυργοσ.def: εὔ-πυργος, ον well-towered, of fortified towns, Il.

ευπωλοσ.def: εὔ-πωλος, ον abounding in foals or horses, Il.: breeding noble horses, Soph.

ευραξ.def: εὐράξ (εὖρος) I. on one side, sideways, Il. II. εὐρὰξ πατάξ, an exclamation to frighten away birds, Ar.

ευρεσισ.def: εὕρεσις, εως (εὑρεῖν) a finding, discovery, Plat.

ευρετεοσ.def: εὑρετέος, η, ον (verb. adj. of εὑρίσκω,) to be discovered, found out, Thuc.

ευρετησ.def: εὑρετής, οῦ, (εὑρεῖν) an inventor, discoverer, Plat.

ευρετικοσ.def: εὑρετικός, ή, όν (εὑρεῖν) inventive, ingenious, Plat.

ευρετοσ.def: εὑρετός, ή, όν (verb. adj. of εὑρίσκω,) discoverable, Xen.

ευρημα.def: εὕρημα, ατος, τό, (εὑρεῖν) I. an invention, discovery, Eur., Ar., etc. 2. c. gen. an invention, for or against a thing, a remedy, Eur., Dem. II. that which is found unexpectedly, i. e., much like Ἕρμαιον, a piece of good luck, godsend, windfall, prize, Hdt., Eur., etc. III. of a child, a foundling, Soph., Eur.

ευρησιεπησ.def: εὑρησι-επής, ές (ἔπος) inventive of words, fluent, Pind.: wordy, sophistical, Ar.

ευριπιδειοσ.def: Εὐρῑπίδειος, η, ον of or like Euripides, Plat.

ευριπιδιον.def: Εὐρῑπίδιον, ου, τό, little Euripides, term of endearment, Ar.

ευριποσ.gloss: a place where the flux and reflux is strong
ευριποσ.def: εὔ-ρῑπος, ὁ, (ῥιπίζω) I. a place where the flux and reflux is strong, esp. the strait which separates Euboea from Boeotia, where the current was said to change seven times a day, Xen.:—proverb of an unstable man, Aeschin. II. generally, a canal, ditch, Anth.

ευρισ.def: εὔ-ρῑς, ῑνος, ὁ, ἡ, (ῥίς) with a good nose, i. e. keen-scented, Aesch., Soph.

ευρισκω.def: εὑρίσκω I. to find, Hom., etc.:—c. part. to find that, Hdt.; and in Pass., ἢν εὑρεθῆις δίκαιος ὤν Soph. 2. c. inf., εὕρισκε πρῆγμά οἱ εἶναι found that the thing for him was, Hdt. II. to find out, discover, Hom., etc.; cf. εὕρημα II:—so in Mid. to find out for oneself, Od. III. to devise, invent, Aesch., etc.:—Mid., τὰ δ’ ἔργα τοὺς λόγους εὑρίσκεται deeds make themselves words, i. e. speak for themselves, Soph. IV. to find, get, gain, procure, Pind., Soph., etc.:—Mid. to get for oneself, bring on oneself, κακὸν εὕρετο Od.; αὐτὸς εὑρόμην πόνους Aesch. V. of merchandise, to find a purchaser, to fetch, earn, πολλὸν χρυσίον εὑροῦσα having fetched a large sum, Hdt.; ἀποδίδοται τοῦ εὑρόντος sells for what it will fetch, Xen.

ευροεω.def: εὐροέω (εὔροος) I. to flow well or abundantly; metaph. to go on well, be favourable, Eur. II. to be fluent, speak successfully, Plut.

ευροια.def: εὔροια, ἡ, I. a good flow, free passage, Plat. II. fluency, id. III. successful progress, id.

ευροκλυδων.def: εὐρο-κλύδων, ωνος, in Act. Ap., probably a storm from the East; but the prob. reading is εὐρ-ακύλων, Euro-aquilo, a N. E. wind.

ευροποσ.def: εὔ-ροπος, ον (ῥέπω) easily inclining, easy-sliding, Anth.

ευροσ.def: Εὖρος, ὁ, the East wind, or more exactly E. S. E., Lat. Eurus, Il. (Probably akin to ἠώς, ἕως, the morning-wind, as Ζέφυρος is to ζόφος, the evening-wind.)
εὖρος breadth, width, absol., εὖρος in breadth, Od., Hdt., etc.; so, τὸ εὖρος Xen.; εἰς εὖρος Eur.

ευρρεησ.def: ἐϋρ-ρεής, ές (ῥέω) fair-flowing, epic gen. ἐϋρρεῖος ποταμοῖο, contr. for ἐϋρρεέος, Il.

ευρρηνοσ.def: ἐΰρ-ρηνος, ον (ῥήν) of a good sheep, Anth.

ευρρουσ.def: ἐΰρ-ρους, ουν I. flowing well or plentifully, fair-flowing, Il., Soph., Eur. II. of words, flowing, fluent, glib, id.

ευρυαγυια.def: εὐρυάγυια (fem. adj. used only in nom. and acc.) with wide streets, in epith. of great cities, Hom.

ευρυαλοσ.def: εὐρύ-ᾰλος, ον (ἅλως) with wide threshing-floor, generally, broad, Anth.

ευρυθμια.def: εὐρυθμία, ἡ, rhythmical order or movement, Plat., etc.

ευρυθμοσ.def: εὔ-ρυθμος, ον 1. rhythmical, of musical time or cadence, Ar., etc. 2. well-proportioned, Xen.; of armour, fitting well, id.

ευρυκρειων.def: εὐρυ-κρείων, οντος, ὁ, wide-ruling, of Agamemnon, Hom.

ευρυμετωποσ.def: εὐρυ-μέτωπος, ον broad-fronted, of oxen, Hom.

ευρυνω.def: εὐρύνω (εὐρύς) 1. to broaden, εὐρῦναι ἀγῶνα to clear the arena (for dancing), Od.; τὸ μέσον εὐρύνειν to leave a wide space in the middle, Hdt. 2. metaph. to extend, Anth.:—Pass. to be spread abroad, Luc.

ευρυοδεια.def: εὐρυ-όδεια, ης, ἡ, (ὁδός) fem. adj. with broad, open ways, only used in gen. fem., χθονὸς εὐρυοδείης Hom.

ευρυοπα.def: εὐρύοπα (ὄψομαι) the far-seeing, of Zeus, εὐρύοπα Ζεύς Hom.; also in voc., εὐρύοπα Ζεῦ Il.;—in Il. there is also an acc. (as if from a nom. εὐρύοψ) εὐρύοπα Ζῆνα.

ευρυπεδοσ.def: εὐρύ-πεδος, ον (πέδον) with broad surface, Anth.

ευρυποροσ.def: εὐρύ-πορος, ον with broad ways, of the sea, where all may roam at will, Hom., etc.

ευρυπυλησ.def: εὐρυ-πῠλής, ές (πύλη) with broad gates, Hom.

ευρυρεεθροσ.def: εὐρυ-ρέεθρος, ον (ῥέεθρον) with broad channel, broadflowing, Il.

ευρυρεων.def: εὐρυρέων (ῥέω) broad-flowing, Il. —there is no such verb as εὐρυρέω, v. εὖ fin.

ευρυσ.def: εὐρύς I. wide, broad, Hom., etc. 2. far-reaching, far-spread, κλέος εὐρύ Od.; ἐλπίδες Anth. II. as adv. the neut. εὐρύ is mostly used, Il., etc.

ευρυσακησ.def: εὐρυ-σᾰ́κης, ες (σάκος) with broad shield, name of Ajax' son, Soph.

ευρυσθενησ.def: εὐρυ-σθενής, ές (σθένος) of far-extended might, mighty, Hom., Pind.

ευρυσοροσ.def: εὐρύ-σορος, ον with wide bier or tomb, Anth.

ευρυφαρετρησ.def: εὐρῠ-φᾰρέτρης, ου, (φαρέτρα) with wide quiver, Pind.

ευρυφυησ.def: εὐρῠ-φυής, ές (φύομαι) broad-growing, of the manner in which the grains of barley are set on the stalk, Od.

ευρυχαδησ.def: εὐρυχᾰδής, ές (χαδεῖν) wide-mouthed, of cups, Anth.

ευρυχαιτησ.def: εὐρυ-χαίτης, ου, with wide-streaming hair, Pind.

ευρυχοροσ.def: εὐρύ-χορος, ον (epic for εὐρύχωρος,) with broad places, spacious, of cities, Hom., etc.: cf. καλλίχορος.

ευρυχωρια.def: εὐρυχωρία, ἡ, 1. open space, free room, Hdt., Dem. 2. of an open field for battle, Xen.; ἐν εὐρυχωρίῃ ναυμαχέειν to fight with plenty of sea-room, Hdt.

ευρωεισ.def: εὐρώεις, εσσα, εν (εὐρώς) mouldy, dank, οἰκία εὐρώεντα (Virgil's loca senta situ), of the world below, Hom.; τάφον εὐρώεντα Soph.

ευρωπη.def: Εὐρώπη, ἡ, Europa, Europe, as a geograph. name, first in the Hhymn. to Apollo.

ευρωποσ.def: εὐρ-ωπός, ή, όν (εὐρύς, ὤψ) (poet. for εὐρύς, Eur.)

ευρωσ.def: εὐρώς, ῶτος, mould, dank decay, Lat. situs, squalor, Theogn., Eur., etc.

ευρωστια.def: εὐρωστία, ἡ, stoutness, strength, Plut. (from εὔρωστος)

ευρωστοσ.def: εὔ-ρωστος, ον (ῥώννυμι) stout, strong, Xen. adv. -τως, id.

ευρωτιαω.def: εὐρωτιάω, (εὐρώς) to be or become mouldy, βίος εὐρωτιῶν the life of the unwashed, Ar.

ευσ.def: ἐύς (epic neut. ἠΰ (εὖ being used only as adv.)) (v. εὖ) good, brave, noble, Hom.:—epic gen. pl. ἐάων, of good things, good fortune, id.

ευσαρκοσ.def: εὔσαρκος, ον (σάρξ) fleshy, in good case, plump, Xen.

ευσεβεια.gloss: reverence towards the gods, piety, religion
ευσεβεια.def: εὐσέβεια 1. reverence towards the gods, piety, religion, Trag.; εὐς. Ζηνός towards him, Soph.; πρὸς εὐσέβειαν εὐσεβῶς, id.:—also, like Lat. pietas, reverence towards parents, filial respect, Plat. 2. credit or character for piety, Soph. (from εὐσεβής)

ευσεβεω.def: εὐσεβέω, to live or act piously and religiously, Theogn., Soph., etc.; εἴς τινα towards one, id.; εὐς. τὰ πρὸς θεούς in matters that respect the gods, id.:—also, εὐς. θεούς to reverence Them, Aesch. (from εὐσεβής)

ευσεβησ.def: εὐ-σεβής, ές (σέβω) I. Lat. pius, pious, religious, Theogn., Hdt., attic; εὐσεβὴς χεῖρα righteous in act, Aesch. II. of acts, things, etc., holy, hallowed, held sacred, id., Eur.:— εὐσεβές [ἐστι], c. inf., Anth.; so, ἐν εὐσεβεῖ [ἐστι] Eur.:— τὸ εὐς. εὐσέβεια, Soph., etc. III. adv. εὐσεβέως, attic -βῶς, Pind., etc.; εὐσεβῶς ἔχει, for εὐσεβές ἐστι, Soph.:—comp. -έστερον, Xen.: Sup. -έστατα, Isocr.

ευσελμοσ.gloss: well-benched, with good banks of oars
ευσελμοσ.def: εὔσελμος (σέλμα) well-benched, with good banks of oars, Hom., Eur.

ευσεπτοσ.def: εὔ-σεπτος, ον (σέβω) much reverenced, holy, Soph.

ευσημοσ.def: εὔ-σημος, ον (σῆμα) I. of good signs or omens, Eur. II. easily known by signs, clear to be seen, Aesch. 2. clear to understand, distinct, Soph.

ευσθενεω.def: εὐσθενέω, to be strong, healthy, Eur. (from εὐσθενής)

ευσιπυοσ.def: εὐ-σίπῠος, ον (σῐπύα) with full bread-basket, Anth.

ευσκανδιξ.def: εὐ-σκάνδιξ, ῑκος, ὁ, ἡ, abounding in chervil, Anth.

ευσκευεω.def: εὐσκευέω, (as if from εὔσκευος) to be well equipt, Soph.

ευσκοποσ.def: εὔσκοπος (σκοπέω) I. sharp-seeing, keen-sighted, watchful, Hom. 2. far-seen or commanding a wide view, Xen. II. （σκοπός) shooting well, of unerring aim, Orac. ap. Hdt., Aesch.

ευσοια.def: εὔσοια, ἡ, happiness, prosperity, Soph. (from εὔσους)

ευσουσ.def: εὔ-σους, ουν safe and well, happy, Theocr.

ευσπειρησ.def: εὐ-σπειρής, ές (σπεῖρα) well-turned, wreathing, winding, Anth.

ευσπλαγχνια.def: εὐσπλαγχνία good heart, firmness, Eur. (from εὔσπλαγχνος)

ευσπλαγχνοσ.def: εὔ-σπλαγχνος, ον I. with healthy bowels, Medic. II. metaph. compassionate, NTest.

ευσταθεια.def: εὐστάθεια stability: good health, vigour, Anth. (from εὐσταθής)

ευσταθεω.def: εὐσταθέω, to be steady, favourable, Eur.:— to be calm, tranquil, of the sea, Luc. (from εὐστᾰθής)

ευσταλεια.def: εὐστάλεια, ἡ, light equipment, Plut. (from εὐστᾰλής)

ευσταλησ.def: εὐ-στᾰλής, ές (στέλλω) 1. well-equipt, Aesch.; of troops, light-armed, Lat. expeditus, Thuc., Xen. 2. well-conducted, favourable, Soph. 3. well-packed, compact, Plut. 4. well-behaved, mannerly, Plat.: —in dress, neat, trim, Luc.

ευσταχυσ.def: εὔσταχυς rich in corn, Anth.: metaph. blooming, fruitful, Anth.

ευστεφανοσ.def: εὐστέφανος I. well-crowned or well-girdled, Hom., Hes. II. crowned with walls and towers, Od., Pind.

ευστομαχοσ.def: εὐστόμᾰχος, ον with good stomach: adv., -χως, Anth.

ευστομεω.def: εὐστομέω, 1. to sing sweetly, Soph. 2. generally, = εὐφημέω, to refrain from speech, Aesch., Ar. (from εὔστομος)

ευστομοσ.def: εὔ-στομος, ον (στόμα) I. with mouth of good size, of dogs, Xen. II. speaking well, eloquent, Anth.; of the cup, making eloquent, id. 2. like εὔφημος, avoiding words of ill omen, περὶ τούτων εὔστομα κείσθω on these things let me keep a religious silence, Hdt.; εὔστομ’ ἔχε peace, be still! Soph.

ευστορθυγξ.def: εὐστόρθυγξ from a good trunk, Anth.

ευστουσ.def: εὔ-στους, ουν (στοά) with goodly colonnades, Anth.

ευστοχια.gloss: skill in shooting at a mark, good aim
ευστοχια.def: εὐστοχία, ἡ, I. skill in shooting at a mark, good aim, Eur.; χερὸς εὐστ., periphr. for a bow, id. II. metaph. quickness in guessing, sagacity, Arist.

ευστοχοσ.def: εὔ-στοχος, ον I. well-aimed, Eur., Xen. II. aiming well, id.:—adv., εὐστόχως βάλλειν id. 2. metaph. guessing well, sagacious, Arist.

ευστρα.gloss: the place for singeing slaughtered swine
ευστρα.def: εὔστρα (εὕω) the place for singeing slaughtered swine, Ar.

ευστρεπτοσ.def: εὔστρεπτος (στρέφω) I. well-twisted, of ropes, Od. II. well-plied, nimble, πόδες Anth.

ευστρεφησ.def: ἐϋ-στρεφής, ές (στρέφω) well-twisted, of cords, Hom.

ευστροφοσ.def: εὔστροφος (στρέφω) I. well-twisted, Il. II. easily turning, active, nimble, Eur.

ευστρωτοσ.def: εὔστρωτος well spread with clothes, Hhymn.

ευστυλοσ.def: εὔ-στῡλος, ον with goodly pillars, Eur.

ευσυμβολοσ.def: εὐσύμβολος I. easy to divine or understand (cf. συμβάλλω III), Aesch. II. easy to deal with, honest, upright, Xen. III. （σύμβολον) affording a good omen, auspicious, Plut.

ευσυνετοσ.def: εὐσύνετος I. quick of apprehension, Arist.:—adv. -τως, with intelligence, comp. -τώτερον, Thuc. II. easily understood, Eur.

ευσυνοπτοσ.gloss: easily taken in at a glance, seen at once
ευσυνοπτοσ.def: εὐ-σύνοπτος, ον (συνόψομαι) easily taken in at a glance, seen at once, Aeschin., etc.

ευσφυροσ.def: εὔσφυρος (σφυρόν) with beautiful ankles, Hes., Eur.

ευσχημοσ.def: εὔ-σχημος, ον (= εὐσχήμων) adv. -μως, with decency, Eur.

ευσχημοσυνη.def: εὐσχημοσύνη, ἡ, gracefulness, decorum, Xen., Plat.

ευσχημων.gloss: elegant in figure, mien and bearing, graceful
ευσχημων.def: εὐ-σχήμων, ονος, (σχῆμα) I. elegant in figure, mien and bearing, graceful, Plat.; comp. -έστερος; Sup. -έστατος, id., Xen. 2. in bad sense, with an outside show of goodness, specious, Eur. II. of things, decent, becoming, id., etc.; τὸ εὔσχημον, Lat. decorum, Plat.:—adv. -μόνως, with grace and dignity, like a gentleman, Ar., Xen. III. noble, honourable, in rank, NTest.

ευσωματεω.gloss: to be well-grown, to be strong and lusty
ευσωματεω.def: εὐσωμᾰτέω, (as if from εὐσώματος) to be well-grown, to be strong and lusty, Eur., Ar.

ευσωτροσ.def: εὔσωτρος with good felloes (σῶτρα), i. e. with good wheels, Hes.

ευτακησ.def: εὐ-τᾰκής, ές (τήκω) easy to soften by heat, Luc.

ευτακτεω.def: εὐτακτέω, to be orderly, behave well, Thuc., Xen., etc.: of soldiers, to obey discipline, id. (from εὔτακτος)

ευτακτοσ.def: εὔ-τακτος, ον I. well-ordered, orderly, Ar. 2. of soldiers, orderly, well-disciplined, id., Thuc., etc. II. adv. -τως, in order, Aesch., Ar.: comp. -ότερον Dem., -τέρως Xen.

ευταξια.def: εὐταξία, ἡ, (from εὔτακτος) 1. good arrangement, good condition, Xen. 2. good order, discipline, Thuc.

ευτε.def: εὖτε relat. adv.: I. of Time, poet. for ὅτε, when, at the time when: 2. with Opt., whenever, referring to instances in past time, Hes., Aesch. 3. with Subj., εὖτ’ ἄν, like ὅταν, whenever, so often as, Od. II. Causal, since, seeing that, Soph. III. as adv. of Comparison, for ἠΰτε, as, even as, twice in Hom.

ευτειχησ.def: εὐτειχής, ές (=εὐτείχεος, Pind., Eur.) (in Il. the acc. is εὐτείχεα, not εὐτειχέα.)

ευτεκνια.gloss: the blessing of children, a breed of goodly children
ευτεκνια.def: εὐτεκνία, ἡ, the blessing of children, a breed of goodly children, Eur.

ευτεκνοσ.def: εὔ-τεκνος, ον (τέκνον) blest with children, Eur., etc.; εὔτ. χρησμός an oracle that gives promise of fair children, id.; εὔτ. ξυνωρίς a pair of fair children, id.: —Sup. -ώτατος id.

ευτελεια.def: εὐτέλεια I. cheapness, Hdt.; εἰς εὐτέλειαν cheaply, i. e. vilely, Ar. II. thrift, economy, ἐπ’ εὐτελείᾳ economically, id.; μετ’ εὐτελείας Thuc.; εἰς εὐτ. συντέμνειν to cut down to an economical standard, id. (from εὐτελής)

ευτελησ.def: εὐ-τελής, ές (τέλος) I. easily paid for, cheap, Hdt., Plat., etc.; εὐτελέστερα δὲ τὰ δεινά the danger would be more cheaply met, Thuc.:—adv. -λῶς, at a cheap rate, Xen. 2. mean, paltry, worthless, Aesch.; εὐτελεστέρα ἄσκησις paltry, requiring no exertion, Xen. II. thrifty, frugal, id.

ευτεχνια.def: εὐ-τεχνία, ἡ, skill in art, Luc., Anth. (from εὔτεχνος)

ευτμητοσ.def: ἐΰ-τμητος, ον (τέμνω) well-cut, of leatherwork, Il.

ευτοκια.def: εὐτοκία, ἡ, happy child-birth, Anth. (from εὔτοκος)

ευτοκοσ.def: εὔ-τοκος, ον (τίκτω) bringing forth easily, Arist.

ευτολμια.def: εὐτολμία, ἡ, courage, boldness, Eur. (from εὔτολμος)

ευτολμοσ.def: εὔ-τολμος, ον (τόλμα) brave-spirited, courageous, Aesch., Xen. adv. -μως, Tyrtae., Aesch.

ευτονοσ.def: εὔ-τονος, ον (τείνω) well-strung, vigorous, Plat.:—adv. -νως, vigorously, Ar.

ευτορνοσ.def: εὔ-τορνος, ον well-turned, rounded, circular, Eur.

ευτραπελια.def: εὐτρᾰπελία, ἡ, 1. wit, liveliness, Lat. urbanitas, Arist., Plut. 2. in bad sense, jesting, ribaldry, NTest.

ευτραπελοσ.def: εὐ-τράπελος, ον (τρέπω) 1. easily turning or changing, λόγος εὐτρ. a dexterous, ready plea, Ar.:—adv. -λως, dexterously, without awkwardness, Thuc. 2. ready with an answer, witty, Lat. lepidus, Arist. b. in bad sense, jesting, ribald, Isocr. 3. tricky, dishonest, Pind.

ευτραφησ.def: εὐ-τρᾰφής, ές (τρέφω) I. well-fed, well-grown, thriving, fat, Eur., etc. II. act. nourishing, Aesch.

ευτρεπησ.def: εὐ-τρεπής, ές (τρέπω) readily turning: generally, ready, Eur.; εὐτρεπὲς ποιεῖσθαί τι id.:—adv., εὐτρεπῶς ἔχειν to be in a state of preparation, Dem.

ευτρεπιζω.def: εὐτρεπίζω, I. to make ready, get ready, ξίφος Aesch., Eur., etc.; εὐτρ. τὰ τείχη to restore them, Xen.:—Pass. to be made ready, Eur.:—Mid. to get ready for oneself, or something of one's own, Thuc. II. to win over, conciliate, τινά τινι Xen.; so in Mid., id.; in perf. pass., ἅπαντας ηὐτρέπισται Dem.

ευτρητοσ.def: εὔτρητος (τιτράω) well-pierced, of ears for earrings, Il.: porous, Anth.

ευτροφια.def: εὐ-τροφία, ἡ, good nurture, thriving condition, Plat.

ευτροχαλοσ.def: εὐτρόχαλος (τρέχω) I. running well, quick-moving, Anth. II. well-rounded, Hes.

ευτροχοσ.def: εὔτροχος I. well-wheeled, Hom., Eur. 2. quick-running, running easily, of a running cord, Xen.; εὔτροχος γλῶσσα a ready, glib tongue, Eur. II. well-rounded, round, Anth.

ευτυκαζομαι.def: εὐτῠκάζομαι, Dep. to make ready, Aesch. (from εὔτῠκος)

ευτυκοσ.def: εὔτῠκος, ον (rare form for εὔτυκτος) ready, Aesch., Theocr.

ευτυκτοσ.def: εὔ-τυκτος, ον (τεύχω) 1. well-made, well-wrought, Hom. 2. ready, Hdt.

ευτυχεω.gloss: to be well off, successful, prosperous
ευτυχεω.def: εὐτῠχέω, (εὐτυχής) 1. to be well off, successful, prosperous, Hdt., etc.; c. part. to succeed in doing, Eur., etc.:— εὐτύχει, like Lat. vale, at the close of letters, etc.; so, ἀλλ’ εὐτυχοίης Trag.:—Pass., ἱκανὰ τοῖς πολεμίοις εὐτύχηται (impers.) they have had success enough, Thuc. 2. of things, to turn out well, prosper, Aesch., Soph., etc.

ευτυχημα.gloss: a piece of good luck, a happy issue, a success
ευτυχημα.def: εὐτύχημα, ατος, τό, (from εὐτῠχέω) a piece of good luck, a happy issue, a success, Eur., Xen., etc.

ευτυχησ.gloss: well off, successful, lucky, fortunate, prosperous
ευτυχησ.def: εὐ-τῠχής, ές (τυγχάνω) I. well off, successful, lucky, fortunate, prosperous, Hdt., attic; εὐτ. ἱκέσθαι τινί to come with blessings to him, Soph.:— τὸ εὐτυχές, εὐτυχία, Thuc. II. adv. -χῶς, Pind., Trag., etc.; ionic -χέως, Hdt.: comp. -έστερον, Eur., etc.; Sup. -έστατα, Hdt.

ευτυχια.def: εὐτῠχία, ἡ, (from εὐτῠχής) good luck, success, prosperity, Hdt., Trag., etc.; εὐτυχίᾳ χρῆσθαι Plat.:—in pl. successes, Thuc.

ευυδροσ.def: εὔ-υδρος, ον (ὕδωρ) 1. well-watered, abounding in water, Pind., Hdt. 2. of a river, with beautiful water, Eur.

ευυμνοσ.def: εὔ-υμνος, ον celebrated in hymns, Hhymn.

ευφαρετρησ.def: εὐ-φᾰρέτρης, ου, (φαρέτρα) with beautiful quiver, Soph.

ευφημεω.gloss: to use words of good omen
ευφημεω.def: εὐφημέω (εὔφημος) to use words of good omen, opp. to δυσφημέω: I. to avoid all unlucky words, Horace's male ominatis parcere verbis: hence, to keep a religious silence, Il., Hdt., etc.; Imperat., εὐφήμει, εὐφημεῖτε hush! be still! Lat. favete linguis, Ar., Plat. II. to shout in praise or honour of any one, or in triumph, Aesch., Ar. 2. c. acc. to honour by praise, speak well of, Xen. III. to sound triumphantly, Aesch.

ευφημια.gloss: the use of words of good omen
ευφημια.def: εὐφημία, ἡ, (from εὔφημος) the use of words of good omen, opp. to δυσφημία: I. abstinence from inauspicious language, religious silence, Trag.; εὐφημίαν ἴσχε = εὐφήμει, Soph.; εὐφημία ’στω, a proclamation of silence before a prayer, Ar. (:dnum [II.] in positive sense, auspiciousness, fairness, Aeschin.:—esp. a fair name for a bad thing, euphemism, id.) III. prayer and praise, worship, honour, Eur.; in pl. songs of praise, lauds, Pind.

ευφημοσ.def: εὔφημος (φήμη) I. uttering sounds of good omen, or abstaining from inauspicious words, i. e. religiously silent, opp. to δύσφημος, Aesch., etc.; εὐφήμου στόμα φροντίδος ἱέντες uttering words of religious thought, i. e. keeping a holy silence, Soph.; so, ὑπ’ εὐφήμου βοῆς, i. e. in silence, id.; εὔφημα φώνει, like εὐφήμει, id. II. in positive sense, auspicious, Aesch., Eur., etc.:—so adv. -μως, with or in words of good omen, Hhymn., Aesch.

ευφθογγοσ.def: εὔ-φθογγος, ον well-sounding, cheerful, Theogn., Aesch.

ευφιλησ.def: εὐ-φῐλής, ές (φιλέω) I. well-loved, Aesch. II. act. loving well, c. gen., id.

ευφιλοπαισ.def: εὐφιλόπαις the children's darling, of a lion's whelp, Aesch.

ευφλεκτοσ.def: εὔ-φλεκτος, ον (φλέγω) easily set on fire, Xen.

ευφορητοσ.def: εὐ-φόρητος, ον easily borne, endurable, τινι Aesch.

ευφορμιγξ.def: εὐ-φόρμιγξ, ιγγος, ὁ, ἡ, with beautiful lyre or playing beautifully on it, Anth.

ευφοροσ.def: εὔ-φορος, ον (φέρω) I. well or patiently borne, Pind. 2. easy to bear or wear, manageable, light, ὅπλα Xen. 3. spreading rapidly, of diseases, Luc. II. act. bearing well; of a breeze, favourable, Xen. 2. of the body, active, vigorous, id. 3. able to endure, patient; adv., εὐφόρως Soph.

ευφραδησ.def: εὐ-φρᾰδής, ές (φράζω) well-expressed: adv., εὐφραδέως ἀγορεύειν to speak in set terms, eloquently, Od.

ευφραδιη.def: εὐφρᾰδίη, ἡ, (ionic and poet. for εὐφράδεια, Anth.)

ευφραινω.def: εὐφραίνω I. to cheer, delight, gladden, Hom., Trag., etc. II. Pass. to make merry, enjoy oneself, be happy, Od., Hdt.; ἐπί τινι Ar.; ἔν τινι, διά τινος, ἀπό τινος Xen.; c. part., εὐφράνθη ἰδών was rejoiced at seeing, Pind.

ευφραστοσ.def: εὔ-φραστος, ον (φράζω) easy to speak or utter, Arist.

ευφρονεων.def: εὐφρονέων well-meaning, well-judging, Hom. No Verb εὐφρονέω occurs.

ευφρονη.def: εὐφρόνη, ἡ, (εὔφρων) the kindly time, euphem. for νύξ, night, Hes., Hdt., etc.

ευφροσυνη.def: εὐφροσύνη (εὔφρων) mirth, merriment, Od.:—of a banquet, good cheer, festivity, id.:—in pl. glad thoughts, id.; festivities, Aesch., etc.

ευφροσυνοσ.def: εὐφρόσυνος (poet. for εὔφρων) adv. -νως, in good cheer, Theogn.

ευφρων.def: εὔφρων (φρήν) I. cheerful, gladsome, merry, of persons making merry, Hom., etc.: adv. εὐφρόνως, with good cheer, Pind., etc. 2. act. cheering, making glad or merry, Il., Aesch., etc. II. later, well-minded, favourable, gracious, Pind., Aesch., etc.:—adv., in this sense, id. III. = εὔφημος, id.

ευφυησ.def: εὐ-φυής, ές (φυή) I. well-grown, shapely, goodly, Il., Eur. II. of good natural disposition, Xen.; of horses and dogs, id. 2. naturally suited or adapted, εἴς or πρός τι Plat.; c. inf., εὐφυὴς λέγειν Aeschin.:— adv. εὐφυῶς Dem. III. of good natural parts, clever, Arist.:—adv. εὐφυῶς, Plat.

ευφυια.def: εὐφυΐα, ἡ, (from εὐφυής) I. natural goodness of shape, shapeliness, Plut. II. good natural parts, cleverness, genius, and morally, goodness of disposition, Arist.

ευφυλακτοσ.def: εὐ-φύλακτος, ον (φυλάσσω) easy to keep or guard, Aesch.:— ἐν εὐφυλάκτῳ εἶναι to be on one's guard, Eur.; εὐφυλακτότερα αὐτοῖς ἐγίγνετο it was easier for them to keep a look-out, Thuc.

ευφωνια.def: εὐφωνία, ἡ, goodness of voice, Xen. (from εὔφωνος)

ευφωνοσ.def: εὔφωνος (φωνή) 1. sweet-voiced, musical, Pind., Aesch. 2. loud-voiced, of a herald, Xen., Dem.

ευχαιτησ.def: εὐ-χαίτης, ου, (χαίτη) with beautiful hair: of trees, with beautiful leaves, Anth.

ευχαλκοσ.def: εὔ-χαλκος, ον wrought of fine brass or well-wrought in brass, Hom., Aesch.

ευχαρισ.def: εὔχαρις pleasing, engaging, winning, gracious, popular, Eur., Plat.:— τὸ εὔχαρι popularity, urbanity, Xen.

ευχαριστεω.def: εὐχᾰριστέω, to be thankful, return thanks, ap. Dem. (from εὐχάριστος)

ευχαριστια.def: εὐχᾰριστία, ἡ, 1. thankfulness, gratitude, Decret. ap. Dem. 2. a giving of thanks. (from εὐχάριστος)

ευχαριστοσ.def: εὐ-χάριστος, ον (χαρίζομαι) I. = εὔχαρις, winning, Xen.: of things, agreeable, pleasant, elegant, id.:—adv., τελευτᾶν τὸν βίον εὐχαρίστως to die happily, Hdt. II. grateful, thankful, Lat. gratus, id., Xen.

ευχειρ.def: εὔχειρ quick or ready of hand, expert, dexterous, Pind., Soph.

ευχειρωτοσ.def: εὐ-χείρωτος, ον (χειρόω) easy to master or overcome, Aesch., Xen.

ευχερεια.def: εὐχέρεια, ἡ, I. dexterity, Plat., etc. II. readiness, proneness, εὐχ. πονηρίας proclivity to evil, id. 2. licentiousness, recklessness, Aesch.

ευχερησ.gloss: easily handled, easy to deal with, easy
ευχερησ.def: εὐ-χερής, ές (χείρη) 1. easily handled, easy to deal with, easy, εὐχερές ἐστι, c. inf., Batr.; πάντα ταῦτ’ ἐν εὐχερεῖ ἔθου didst make light of them, Soph.:—adv. -ρῶς, id. 2. of persons, manageable, accommodating, kind, yielding, Soph.:—adv., εὐχερῶς φέρειν Plat., etc.; comp. -έστερον, Xen. 3. in bad sense, unscrupulous, reckless, Dem.:—adv. -ρῶς, id.

ευχεταομαι.def: εὐχετάομαι, (only in epic pres. and imperf. εὐχετόωνται, -όωντο, inf. -άασθαι) (εὔχομαι) Dep. I. to pray, Il.; to make vows, Hom. II. to boast oneself, profess, brag, boast, c. inf., τίνες ἔμμεναι εὐχετόωνται; Od., etc.; ἐπ’ ἀνδράσιν εὐχ. to glory over them, id.

ευχη.def: εὐχή, ἡ, (εὔχομαι) 1. a prayer, vow, Od., etc.: (but the common Homeric words are εὖχος and εὐχωλή); εὐχὴν ἐπιτελέσαι, Lat. vota persolvere, Hdt.; ἀποδιδόναι Xen.; κατὰ χιλίων εὐχὴν ποιήσασθαι χιμάρων to make a vow of a thousand goats, Ar. 2. a mere wish, an aspiration, as opp. to reality, εὐχαῖς ὅμοια λέγειν to build castles in the air, Plat. 3. a prayer for evil, i. e. an imprecation, Aesch., Eur.

ευχιλοσ.def: εὔ-χῑλος, ον of a horse, feeding well, Xen.

ευχιμαροσ.def: εὐ-χῐ́μᾰρος, ον rich in goats, Anth.

ευχομαι.gloss: to pray, offer prayers, pay one's vows, make a vow
ευχομαι.def: εὔχομαι (v. sub fin.) Dep.: I. to pray, offer prayers, pay one's vows, make a vow, Lat. precari, vota facere, θεῶι or θεοῖς Hom., etc.; πρὸς τοὺς θεούς Xen., etc.:—c. dat. commodi, to pray for one, Il. 2. c. inf. to pray that, Hom., etc.; also, εὔχ. τοὺς θεοὺς δοῦναι to pray them to give, Xen. 3. c. acc. objecti, to pray for a thing, long or wish for, Pind., attic; εὔχ. τινί τι to pray for something for a person, as Soph. II. to vow or promise to do, c. inf., Hom., attic 2. c. acc. rei, like Lat. vovere, to vow a thing, Aesch., Ar. III. to profess loudly, to boast, vaunt, Il.; mostly of something of which one has a right to be proud, πατρὸς ἐξ ἀγαθοῦ γένος εὔχομαι εἶναι id. 2. simply to profess or declare, Od. IV. as a Pass., ἐμοὶ μετρίως εὖκται I have prayed sufficiently, Plat.:—but Soph. uses plup. ηὔγμην in act. sense.

ευχοσ.gloss: the thing prayed for, object of prayer
ευχοσ.def: εὖχος, εος, (εὔχομαι) I. the thing prayed for, object of prayer, εὖχος δοῦναι, πορεῖν to grant one's prayer, Hom.; εὖχος ἀρέσθαι to obtain it, Il. II. a boast, vaunt, id., Pind. III. a vow, votive offering, Anth.

ευχρηστοσ.gloss: easy to make use of, useful, serviceable
ευχρηστοσ.def: εὔ-χρηστος, ον (χράομαι) easy to make use of, useful, serviceable, Xen., etc.

ευχροησ.def: εὐ-χροής, ές (epic for εὔχροος) δέρμα βόειον ἐϋχροές Od.

ευχρουσ.gloss: well-coloured, of good complexion, fresh-looking, healthy
ευχρουσ.def: εὔ-χρους, ουν (χρόα) well-coloured, of good complexion, fresh-looking, healthy, Xen., etc.:—comp. -οώτερος, id.

ευχρυσοσ.def: εὔ-χρῡσος, ον rich in gold, of the Pactolus, Soph.

ευχωλη.def: εὐχωλή, ἡ, (εὔχομαι) (epic form of εὐχή) I. a prayer, vow, Hom. II. a boast, vaunt, Il.: a shout of triumph, id. 2. an object of boasting, a boast, glory, κὰδ δέ κεν εὐχωλὴν Πριάμῳ λίποιεν Ἑλένην id.

ευχωλιμαιοσ.def: εὐχωλῐμαῖος, η, ον (from εὐχωλή) bound by a vow, Hdt.

ευψυχεω.def: εὐψῡχέω, I. to be of good courage, NTest. II. imperat. εὐψύχει farewell, Inscr. on tombs, Anth.

ευψυχια.def: εὐψῡχία, ἡ, good courage, high spirit, Aesch., etc. (from εὔψῡχος)

ευψυχοσ.gloss: of good courage, stout of heart, courageous
ευψυχοσ.def: εὔ-ψῡχος, ον (ψυχή) of good courage, stout of heart, courageous, Lat. animosus, Aesch., etc.; τὸ ἐς τὰ ἔργα εὔψυχον Thuc.; εὐψυχότατοι πρὸς τὸ ἐπιέναι id.:— adv. -χως, Xen.

ευω.def: εὕω to singe, of singeing off swine's bristles, Hom.

ευωδησ.def: εὐ-ώδης, ες (ὄδωδα) sweet-smelling, fragrant, Hom., etc.; εὐωδέστατος Hdt.

ευωδια.def: εὐωδία, ἡ, (from εὐώδης) a sweet smell, Hdt., Xen.

ευωδιν.def: εὐ-ώδῑν, ῑνος, ὁ, ἡ, happy as a parent, fruitful, Anth.

ευωνοσ.def: εὔ-ωνος, ον of fair price, cheap (Fr. à bon marché）, Xen., Dem., etc.

ευωνυμοσ.def: εὐ-ώνῠμος, ον (ὄνυμα, aeolic for ὄνομα) I. of good name, honoured, Hes., Pind., etc. 2. of good omen, prosperous, fortunate, id., Plat. II. euphemistic for ἀριστερός (which was a word of ill omen), left, on the left hand, Hdt., Soph., etc.; ἐξ εὐωνύμου χειρός or ἐξ εὐωνύμου, on the left, Hdt.

ευωπισ.def: εὐ-ῶπις, ιδος (ὤψ) fair to look on, Od., Pind.

ευωποσ.def: εὐ-ωπός, όν (= εὐώψ, Eur.) εὐ. πύλαι friendly gates, id.

ευωριαζω.def: εὐωριάζω, to be negligent, Aesch. (from εὔωρος)

ευωροσ.def: εὔ-ωρος, ον (ὤρα) careless, τινος about a thing.

ευωχεω.def: εὐ-ωχέω, (εὖ, ἔχω) I. to treat or feed well, entertain sumptuously, Hdt., attic: —Mid. to fare sumptuously, feast, Hdt.; κρέα εὐωχ. to feast upon, enjoy, Xen.; of animals, to eat their fill, Ar., Xen. II. metaph., εὐωχεῖν τινα καινῶν λόγων to entertain him with novelties, Theophr.: —Mid. to relish, enjoy, c. gen., τοῦ λόγου Plat.

ευωχια.def: εὐωχία, ἡ, (from εὐωχέω) good cheer, feasting, Ar., etc.:—metaph., λόγων εὐωχίαι feasts of reason, Anth.

ευωψ.def: εὐ-ώψ, ῶπος, (ὤψ) fair to look on, Soph.

εφαγιστευω.def: ἐφαγιστεύω fut. σω to perform obsequies over the grave, Soph.

εφαγνιζω.def: ἐφαγνίζω fut. σω (= ἐφαγιστεύω) τὰ πάντ’ ἐφαγνίσαι to perform all the obsequies, Soph.

εφαιρεομαι.def: ἐφαιρέομαι Pass. to be chosen to succeed another, Thuc.

εφαλλομαι.def: ἐφάλλομαι 3rd sg. epic aor2 ἐπ-ᾶλτο part. ἐπ-άλμενος part. ἐπι-άλμενος (cf. ἀναπάλλω) (with part. ἐπ-άλμενος, ἐπι-άλμενος) Dep.:— to spring upon, assail, c. dat., Τρώεσσιν ἐπάλμενος Il.:—also, without hostile sense, c. gen., ἐπιάλμενος ἵππων having leaped upon the chariot, id.

εφαλοσ.def: ἔφ-ᾰλος, ον (ἅλς) on the sea, of seaports, Il., Soph.

εφαμιλλοσ.gloss: a match for, equal to, rivalling
εφαμιλλοσ.def: ἐφ-ᾰ́μιλλος, ον (ἅμιλλα) I. a match for, equal to, rivalling, ἐφ. γίγνεσθαί τινι Xen. II. pass. regarded as an object of rivalry or contention, Dem.

εφανδανω.def: ἐφανδάνω fut. -αδήσω epic ἐπι-ανδάνω to please, be grateful to, c. dat., ἐμοὶ δ’ ἐπιανδάνει οὕτως Il.; τοῖσιν δ’ ἐπιήνδανε μῦθος Od.

εφαπαξ.def: ἐφάπαξ I. once for all, NTest., etc. II. at once, at the same time, id.

εφαπλοω.def: ἐφαπλόω fut. ώσω to spread or fold over, Babr.

εφαπτω.def: ἐφάπτω ionic ἐπ-άπτω fut. ψω I. to bind on or to, λύουσα ἢ ’φάπτουσα undoing or making fast, Soph.; τοὖργον ὡς ἐφάψειεν τόδε that she had made fast (i. e. perpetrated) the deed, id.:—Pass., 3rd sg. perf. and plup. ἐφῆπται, -το, is or was hung over one, impends over, is fixed as one's doom, c. dat., Τρώεσσι κήδε’ ἐφῆπται Il. II. Mid. to lay hold of, grasp, reach, c. gen., Od., Theogn., Soph. 2. to lay hold of with the mind, attain to, Lat. assequi, c. gen., Plat. 3. in Pind. also c. dat. (like θιγγάνω, ψαύω), to apply oneself to. 4. Hdt. uses part. perf. pass. with gen., εἴδεος ἐπαμμένος possessed of a certain degree of beauty. 5. to follow, come next, Theocr.

εφαρμοζω.def: ἐφαρμόζω attic -όττω doric -όσδω fut. -αρμόσω I. intr. to fit on or to, to fit one, c. dat., Il. 2. to be adapted to, τινί Arist. II. trans. to fit one thing to another, fit on, put on, τί τινι Hes., Theocr.:— Mid. to put on oneself, Anth. 2. to suit, accommodate, Xen.; πίστιν ἐφαρμόσαι to add fitting assurance, Soph.

εφαρμοστεοσ.def: ἐφαρμοστέος, ον (from ἐφαρμόζω) (verb. adj.) one must adapt, τί τινι Luc.

εφεδρα.def: ἐφέδρα a sitting by or before a place: a siege, blockade, Lat. obsessio, Hdt.

εφεδρεια.def: ἐφεδρεία, ἡ, I. a sitting upon. II. a sitting by, waiting for one's turn, of pugilists, Plat.: a lying in wait, Plut. (from ἐφεδρεύω)

εφεδρευω.def: ἐφεδρεύω fut. σω (ἔφεδρος) I. to sit upon, rest upon, Eur. II. to lie by or near, lie in wait, of an enemy waiting to attack, Thuc.; ἐφ. τινί to keep watch over, Eur.: generally, to watch for, Dem. III. to halt, Plut.

εφεδρησσω.def: ἐφεδρήσσω poet. for ἐφεδρεύω to sit by, τινί Anth.

εφεδροσ.def: ἔφ-εδρος, ον (ἕδρα) I. sitting or seated upon, c. gen., λεόντων ἔφεδρε, of Cybele, Soph.; ἔφ. ἵππου Eur. II. sitting by, at, or near, τῶν πηδαλίων, of a pilot, Plat.; also c. dat., Eur.: absol. close at hand, Soph. 2. posted in support or reserve, Eur. 3. lying by, of a third combatant (pugilist or wrestler), who sits by to fight the conqueror, Pind., Ar., Xen.:— μόνος ὢν ἔφεδρος δισσοῖς, i. e. one against two, with no one to take his place if beaten, Aesch. 4. a successor, Hdt.

εφεζομαι.def: ἐφέζομαι inf. ἐφέζεσθαι Dep. 1. to sit upon, c. dat., Hom., Ar.;—also c. gen., Pind.; and c. acc., Aesch., Eur. 2. to sit by or near, Od., Aesch.

εφεκτοσ.def: ἔφ-εκτος, ον containing 1+1/6: τόκος ἔφ. when 1/6 of the principal was paid as interest, = 16 2/3 p. cent., Dem.

εφελκω.def: ἐφέλκω ionic ἐπ- fut. ἐφέλξω aor1 ἐφείλκυσα (the aor1in use is ἐφείλκυσα) (cf. ἕλκω) I. to draw on, drag or trail after one, ἐπ. τὰς οὐράς, of long-tailed sheep, Hdt.; ἵππον ἐκ τοῦ βραχίονος ἐπ. to lead a horse by a rein upon the arm, id.; ναῦς ὡς ἐφέλξω will take in tow, Eur. 2. to bring on, bring in its train, id. 3. to drink off, id. II. Pass., ἐφελκομένοισι πόδεσσι with feet trailing after him, of one who is dragged lifeless away, Il.; ἐφέλκετο ἔγχος, i. e. sticking in his hand, id.; ἐπελκόμενος trailing behind, of a boat, Hdt.; οἱ ἐπελκόμενοι the stragglers of an army, id. 2. to be attracted, Hhymn., Thuc. III. Mid. to draw to oneself, attract, αὐτὸς γὰρ ἐφέλκεται ἄνδρα σίδηρος the very sight of arms attracts men, i. e. tempts them to use it, Od. 2. to draw or pull over, Plut.; ἐφ. ὀφρῦς to frown, Anth. 3. to bring on consequences, Eur., Xen. 4. to assume, Plat., Theocr.

εφεξησ.gloss: in order, in a row, one after another
εφεξησ.def: ἐφεξῆς I. in order, in a row, one after another, Hdt., Eur., Xen. 2. c. dat. next to, Plat. II. in succession, without exception, πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐφ. Xen.; τὴν Ἑλλάδα πᾶσαν ἐφ. Dem. 2. of Time, τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐπεξῆς Hdt.; τέσσαρες ἐφ. Ar. 3. thereupon, after, εὐθὺς ἐφ. Dem.

εφεξισ.def: ἔφεξις, εως (ἐπέχω) an excuse, pretext, τοῦ ἔφεξιν; = τίνος χάριν; Ar.

εφεπω.def: ἐφέπω imperf. epic ἔφεπον ionic ἐφέπεσκον fut. ἐφέψω aor2 ἐπέσπον inf. ἐπισπεῖν part. ἐπισπών mid ἐφέπομαι imperf.mid -ειπόμην fut. -έψομαι aor2 -εσπόμην imperat. ἐπί-σπου inf. ἐπι-σπέσθαι I. to go after, follow, pursue, c. acc., Il. II. to drive on, urge on, [ἵππους] ἐφέπων μάστιγι id.; and c. dat. pers., Πατρόκλῳ ἔφεπε ἵππους drove them against him, id. III. to follow a pursuit, busy oneself about it, c. acc., Hom.; ἐφ. Θήβας to administer, govern it, Aesch. 2. c. acc. loci, to search, explore, traverse, Lat. obire, Hom., Hes. IV. to come suddenly upon, encounter, incur, πότμον ἐπισπεῖν Hom.; ὀλέθριον ἦμαρ ἐπ. Il. B. Mid. to follow, pursue, c. dat., Od., Hdt., etc. II. to follow, accompany, attend, Il., Hdt.; ἐπισπέσθαι ποσίν to follow on foot, i. e. keep up with, Hdt.; εἴ οἱ τύχη ἐπίσποιτο if fortune attend him, id.:—absol., Thuc. 2. to obey, attend to, θεοῦ ὀμφῇ Od.; ἐπισπόμενοι μένεϊ σφῷ giving the reins to their passion, id.; βουλῇ ἐπισπέσθαι πατρός Aesch., etc.:—absol., ὁ ἐπισπόμενος, opp. to ὁ πείσας, Thuc.:—also to agree, approve, in tmesi, ἐπὶ δ’ ἕσπωνται θεοὶ ἄλλοι Od. 3. to follow an argument, Plat.

εφερπω.def: ἐφέρπω fut. ψω but the aor1 in use is ἐφείρπῠσα I. to creep upon, Ar. II. poet. to come on or over, come gradually or stealthily upon, τινά Aesch.; ἐπ’ ὄσσοισι νὺξ ἐφέρπει Eur. 2. absol. to go forth, proceed, Aesch.; in part. advancing, future, Pind.

εφεσια.def: Ἐφέσια the feast of Ephesian Artemis, Thuc.

εφεσιμοσ.gloss: in which there was the right of appeal
εφεσιμοσ.def: ἐφέσιμος, δίκη, ἡ, δίκη, a suit in which there was the right of appeal, Dem. (from ἔφεσις)

εφεσισ.def: ἔφεσις, εως (ἐφίημι) I. a throwing or hurling at, a shooting, Plat. 2. as attic law-term, an appeal to another court, Dem. II. （ἐφίεμαι) appetite, desire, Arist.

εφεστιοσ.gloss: at one's own fireside, at home
εφεστιοσ.def: ἐφέστιος (ἑστία) I. at one's own fireside, at home, Od.; ἐφέστιοι ὅσσοι ἔασιν as many as have a home of their own, Il.; ἐφέστιον πῆξαι σκῆπτρον (i. e. ἐπὶ τῇ ἑστίᾳ) Soph.:—of suppliants who claim protection by sitting by the fireside, Hdt.; δόμων ἐφ. an inmate of the temple, Aesch.; also merely of guests, Soph. II. generally, of or in the house or family, Lat. domesticus, πόνοι δόμων ἐφέστιοι Aesch.; ἐφ. δόμοι the chambers of the house, id.:—ionic ἐπίστιον, ου, τό, a household, family, Hdt.: — θεοὶ ἐφ. the household gods, Lat. Lares or Penates, Ζεὺς ἐπίστιος, ἐφέστιος, as presiding over hospitality, id., Soph.

εφεστριδιον.def: ἐφεστρίδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ἐφεστρίς, Luc.)

εφεστρισ.def: ἐφεστρίς, ίδος (ἐφέννυμι) an upper garment, wrapper, Xen., Plut.

εφετησ.def: ἐφέτης, ου, (ἐφίημι) I. a commander, Aesch. II. ἐφέται, οἱ, at Athens, the Ephetae, a court of Eupatridae, created by Draco to try cases of homicide, Plut.

εφετμη.def: ἐφετμή, ἡ, (ἐφίημι) a command, behest, Hom., etc.

εφευρετησ.def: ἐφευρετής, οῦ, an inventor, contriver, NTest. (from ἐφευρίσκω)

εφευρισκω.def: ἐφευρίσκω ionic ἐπ- fut. ἐφευρήσω aor2 ἐφηῦρον aor2 ἐφεῦ I. to light upon, discover, Od.; with a partic. to find one doing so and so, Hom., Soph.:—so in Pass., μὴ ἐπευρεθῇ πρήσσων Hdt. II. to invent or bring in besides, generally to invent, Pind., Eur.

εφεψιαομαι.def: ἐφεψιάομαι Dep. to mock or scoff at, τινι, Lat. illudere, epic 3rd pl. ἐφεψιόωνται Od.

εφηβαω.gloss: to come to man's estate, grow up to manhood
εφηβαω.def: ἐφηβάω ionic ἐπ- fut. ήσω to come to man's estate, grow up to manhood, Hdt., Aesch., Xen.

εφηβεια.def: ἐφηβεία, ἡ, (ἐφηβεύω) puberty, man's estate, Anth.

εφηβευω.def: ἐφηβεύω (ἔφηβος) to arrive at man's estate.

εφηβικοσ.def: ἐφηβικός, ή, όν of or for an ἔφηβος, Theocr. (from ἔφηβος)

εφηβοσ.def: ἔφηβος I. one arrived at puberty (ἥβη) a youth of 18 years when the Athen. youth underwent his δοκιμασία and was registered as a citizen, Xen., etc. II. a throw on the dice, Anth.

εφηβοσυνη.def: ἐφηβοσύνη, ἡ, the age of an ἔφηβος, puberty, Anth.

εφηγεομαι.def: ἐφηγέομαι fut. -ήσομαι Dep. to lead to a place: esp. to lead the magistrate to a house where a criminal lay concealed, Dem.

εφηδομαι.def: ἐφήδομαι Pass. to exult over a person, τινι Xen.

εφηκω.def: ἐφήκω fut. ξω 1. to have arrived, Soph., Thuc. 2. ὅσον ἂν ἡ μόρα ἐφήκῃ so far as the division reaches, so much space as it occupies, Xen.

εφηλιξ.def: ἐφ-ῆλιξ, ῐκος, ὁ, ἡ, (= ἔφηβος, Anth.)

εφημαι.def: ἔφημαι (perf. pass. used as a pres.) (cf. ἧμαι) I. to be set or seated on, to sit on, θρόνῳ Od.; also c. gen., θινὸς ἐφήμενος Soph.:— to be seated at or in, δόμοις Aesch.: —also c. acc., βρέτας ἐφήμενος id. II. to act as assessor (cf. ἔφεδρος), Παλλὰς οἵ τ’ ἐφήμενοι id.

εφημερια.gloss: for the daily service of the temple
εφημερια.def: ἐφημερία, ἡ, ἐφ’ ἡμέραν, for the daily service of the temple, NTest.

εφημεριοσ.def: ἐφημέριος (ἡμέρα) 1. on, for or during the day, the day through, Od.; by day, Pind. 2. for a day only, for the day, ἐφημέρια φρονέοντες taking thought for the day only, Od.:—often of men, ἐφημέριοι creatures of a day, Aesch., etc. 3. hired for the day, Theogn.

εφημερισ.def: ἐφ-ημερίς, ίδος (ἡμέρα) a diary, journal, such as Caesar's Commentarii, Plut.

εφημεροσ.def: ἐφ-ήμερος, ον (ἡμέρα) I. living but a day, short-lived, Pind., Eur., etc. 2. of men, ἐφήμεροι creatures of a day, Pind., Aesch. II. for the day, daily, Plut., etc. III. φάρμακον ἐφ. killing on the same day, id.

εφθημιμερησ.def: ἑφθημιμερής containing seven halves, i. e. 3 1/2, of the first 3 1/2 feet of a Hexameter or Iambic Trimeter.

εφθοσ.def: ἑφθός, ή, όν verb. adj. of ἕψω 1. boiled, dressed, Hdt., Eur., etc. 2. ἑφθὸς χρυσός refined gold, Simon.

εφιζανω.def: ἐφιζάνω (only in pres. and imperf.) to sit at or in a place, c. dat., Il.; ὕπνος ἐπὶ βλεφάροισιν ἐφίζανεν sleep sate upon, id.

εφιζω.def: ἐφίζω doric -ίσδω I. Causal, in epic aor1, to set upon, ἐφέσσαι to set me ashore, Od.:—Mid., γούνασιν οἷσιν ἐφεσσάμενος having set [me] on his knees, id.; imperat., ἔφεσσαί με νηός set me on board the ship, id. II. intr. in pres. and imperf. ἐφῖζον, ionic ἐφίζεσκον, to sit at or by, id., Pind., etc.

εφιημι.def: ἐφίημι ionic ἐπ- fut. ἐφήσω aor1 ind. ἐφῆκα epic ἐφέηκα aor2 imperat. ἔφες subj. ἐφείω, ῃς attic ἐφῇς part. ἐφείς Mid., part. ἐφιέμενος fut. ἐφήσομαι 3rd sg. imperf. ἐφίει (3rd sg. imperf. ἐφίει as if from ἐφιέω) I. to send to one, Il. 2. c. inf. to set on or incite to do, ἐφέηκε ἀεῖσαι Od.; ἐφ. τινὰ χαλεπῆναι, etc., Il. 3. of things, to throw or launch at one, ὅς τοι ἐφῆκε βέλος id., etc.; ἐφ. οἰστὸν ἐπί τινι Eur.; ἐφ. χεῖράς τινι to lay hands on him, Od. 4. of events, destinies, etc., to send upon one, τοῖσιν πότμον ἐφῆκεν Il., etc. 5. to send against, in hostile sense, Hdt., etc.:— ἐφ. τὸν ποταμὸν ἐπὶ τὴν χώρην id.; ἐφῆκας γλῶσσαν did'st let loose, Eur. 6. to throw into, ἐς λέβητ’ ἐφῆκεν μέλη id. II. to let go, loosen, esp. the rein, Plat.:—hence to give up, yield, Lat. concedere, τινὶ τὴν ἡγεμονίαν Thuc.:—c. inf. to permit, allow, τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Hdt., Soph., etc. 2. to give up, leave as a prey, Soph.:—then, seemingly, intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν), to give oneself up to, οὐρίᾳ a fair wind, Plat. III. to put the male to the female, Hdt. IV. as law-term, to leave to another to decide, δίκας ἐφ. εἴς τινα Dem.:—and absol. to appeal, εἰς τοὺς δικαστάς id. B. Mid. to lay one's command or behest upon, Hom., Aesch., etc.:—c. inf., ἐφ. τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Soph., Ar.; ἐς Λακεδαίμονα to send orders to L., Thuc. 2. to allow or permit one to do, Soph., etc. II. c. gen. to aim at, Arist.:— to long after, desire, Soph., Eur., etc.; c. inf. to desire to do, Eur.

εφικνεομαι.def: ἐφικνέομαι ionic ἐπ- fut. ἐφίξομαι aor 2 ἐφῑκόμην ionic ἐπ I. Dep.:— to reach at, aim at, c. gen., Il., Plat., etc. 2. to reach or extend, ἐφ’ ὅσον μνήμη ἐφ. Xen., etc. 3. metaph. to hit or touch the right points, Lat. rem acu tangere, τῷ λόγῳ ἐφ. τῶν ἐκεῖ κακῶν Dem.;—so, ἐς τὰ ἄλλα ἐπίκεο Hdt. 4. to reach, gain, attain to, ἀνδραγαθίας Aeschin., etc. II. c. acc. to come upon, εἴ σε μοῖρ’ ἐφίκοιτο Pind.; dupl. acc., ἐπικέσθαι πληγὰς τὸν Ἑλλήσποντον to visit it with blows, Hdt.

εφικτοσ.def: ἐφικτός, ή, όν (from ἐφικνέομαι) easy to reach, accessible, Plut.

εφιμειρω.def: ἐφιμείρω (strengthd. for ἱμείρω) c. gen., Anth.

εφιμεροσ.def: ἐφ-ῑ́μερος, ον longed for, desired, charming, Hes., Aesch.; c. inf., ἐφ. προσλεύσσειν Soph.

εφιππαζομαι.def: ἐφιππάζομαι Dep. to ride upon, Luc.

εφιππιοσ.def: ἐφ-ίππιος, ον (ἵππος) for putting on a horse, Xen.:— ἐφίππιον (sc. στρῶμα) a saddle-cloth, id.

εφιπποσ.def: ἔφ-ιππος, ον I. on horseback, riding: ἀνδριὰς ἔφ. an equestrian statue, Plut. II. κλύδων ἔφιππος a rushing wave of horses, Soph.

εφιστημι.def: ἐφίστημι ionic ἐπ- A. Causal in pres., imperf., fut., and aor1: I. to set or place upon, τί τινι Thuc.; τι ἐπί τινι Xen.: metaph., ἐφ. μοῖραν βίῳ Plat. II. to set over, Lat. praeficere, ἐφ. τινὰ ὕπαρχόν τισι Hdt., etc. III. to set up, establish, institute games, id. IV. to set by or near to, ἱππέας ἐπιστήσαντες κύκλῳ τὸ σῆμα (= περὶ τὸ ς.) id. V. to stop, make halt, Lat. inhibere, Xen.: —absol., ἐπιστήσας (sc. ἑαυτόν, τὸν ἵππον) having halted, id. VI. ἐφίστημι τὴν γνώμην κατά τι to fix one's mind upon it, attend to it, and then absol. to give attention, Arist. 2. c. acc. pers. to arrest the attention of, Plut. B. intr. in Mid. and Pass., ἐφίσταμαι, aor1 ἐπεστάθην, with perf., plup. and aor2 act.:— to stand upon, πύργῳ, δίφρῳ, ἐπὶ βηλῷ Il. 2. to be imposed upon, τινι Soph. 3. to stand on the top or surface, τὸ ἐπιστάμενον τοῦ γάλακτος, i. e. cream, Hdt. II. to be set over, Lat. praeesse, c. dat., Aesch., etc.; also c. gen., Hdt., Eur.:—absol. to be in authority, Hdt., etc. III. to stand by or near, ἀλλήλοισι Il., etc.: of dreams or visions, to appear to, εὕδοντι ἐπέστη ὄνειρος Hdt. 2. in hostile sense, to stand against, oppose, Hom.: to come upon by surprise, Thuc. 3. of events, to impend, be at hand, Lat. instare, Κῆρες ἐφεστᾶσιν θανάτοιο Il.; πρίν μοι τύχη ἐπέστη Soph. IV. to halt, stop, as in a march, Xen.:— c. gen., ἐπ. τοῦ πλοῦ Thuc. V. to fix one's mind on, give one's attention to, τινι Eur., Dem. C. the aor1 mid. is used in causal sense, to set up, τὰς θύρας Xen.: to set, post, φρουρούς id.

εφοδευω.gloss: to visit, go the rounds, patrol
εφοδευω.def: ἐφοδεύω fut. σω (ἔφοδος) I. to visit, go the rounds, patrol, Xen.:—Pass., ἐφοδεύεται the rounds are made, Ar. II. c. dat. to watch over, ἀγῶσιν Aesch.

εφοδιαζω.gloss: to furnish with supplies for a journey
εφοδιαζω.def: ἐφοδιάζω ionic ἐποδ- fut. άσω (ἐφόδιον) I. to furnish with supplies for a journey, Lat. viaticum dare, Hdt. II. Mid., πενταδραχμίαν ἑκάστῳ ἐφοδιασάμενος having seen that five drachms were paid to each, Xen.:—metaph. to maintain, ἀργίαν Plut.

εφοδιον.def: ἐφόδιον (mostly in pl. ἐφόδια) (ἐφ’ ὁδοῦ) 1., like Lat. viaticum, supplies for travelling, money and provisions, Hdt., Dem.:—of an ambassador's travelling-allowance, Ar.; sometimes in sg., Thuc., Xen. 2. generally, ways and means, maintenance, support, ἐφόδια τῷ γήρᾳ Dem.; of public money, μιᾶς ἡμέρας ἐφόδια ἐν τῷ κοινῷ id.

εφοδοσ.def: ἔφ-οδος, ὁ, one who goes the rounds, Xen.
ἔφ-οδος, ἡ, I. a way towards, approach, Thuc., Xen.:— access for traffic and intercourse, communication, παρ’ ἀλλήλους Thuc. 2. importation, Xen. II. an onset, attack, assault, Aesch., Thuc., etc.

εφολκαιον.def: ἐφόλκαιον, ου, τό, (ἐφέλκω) a rudder, Od.

εφολκιον.def: ἐφόλκιον, ου, τό, (ἐφέλκω) a tow-boat: metaph an appendage, Anth., Plut.

εφολκισ.def: ἐφολκίς, ίδος (= ἐφολκός) a burdensome appendage, Eur.

εφολκοσ.def: ἐφολκός, όν (ἐφέλκω) I. drawing on or towards, enticing, alluring, Thuc. II. requiring to be drawn on, a laggard, Ar.

εφομαρτεω.def: ἐφομαρτέω fut. ήσω to follow close after, Il.

εφοπλιζω.def: ἐφοπλίζω fut. σω epic aor1 inf. ἐφοπλίσσαι 1. to equip, get ready, prepare, Hom.; so in Mid., δόρπα τ’ ἐφοπλισόμεσθα we will get ready our suppers, Il. 2. to arm against, τινά τινι, so in Mid., Anth.

εφορατικοσ.def: ἐφορᾱτικός, ή, όν fit for overlooking, ἔργων Xen. (from ἐφοράω)

εφοραω.def: ἐφοράω ionic 3rd sg. ἐπορᾷ 3rd pl. ἐπορέωσι inf. ἐπορᾶν imperf. ἐφεώρων ionic 3rd sg. ἐπώρα fut. ἐπόψομαι epic also ἐπιόψομαι the aor. is ἐπεῖδον I. to oversee, observe, survey, of the sun, Hom.:—then of the gods, to watch over, observe, take notice of, Od., Hdt., etc.; of a general going his rounds, Thuc.; to visit the sick, Xen. 2. simply, to look upon, view, behold, Od., etc.:—Pass., ὅσον ἐφεωρᾶτο τῆς νήσου as much of it as was in view, Thuc. II. to look out, choose, ἐπιόψομαι ἥτις ἀρίστη Od., etc.

εφορειον.def: ἐφορεῖον, ου, τό, (ἔφορος) the court of the ephors, Xen.

εφορευω.def: ἐφορεύω I. = ἐφοράω, c. acc., Aesch.; c. gen., id. II. to be ephor, Thuc., Xen. (ἔφορος)

εφορικοσ.def: ἐφορικός, ή, όν (ἔφορος) of or for the ephori, Xen.

εφοριοσ.def: ἐφ-όριος, η, ον (ὅρος) on the border or frontier, ap. Dem.

εφορμαω.def: ἐφορμάω ionic ἐπ- fut. ήσω I. to stir up, rouse against one, Hom.; ἐπορμῆσαι τοὺς λύκους to set them on, Hdt.; ναύτας ἐφορμήσαντα τὸ πλεῖν having urged them on to sail, Soph. II. intr. to rush upon, attack, τινί Eur. III. Pass. and Mid. to be stirred up; c. inf. to be eager or desire to do, Hom.:—absol. to rush furiously on, ἔγχει ἐφορμᾶσθαι Il.; ἐφορμηθείς id.; and, without hostile sense, to spring forward, Od.:— c. acc. to rush upon, make a dash at, Il.

εφορμεω.def: ἐφορμέω ionic ἐπ- fut. ήσω 1. to lie moored at or over against a place, to blockade it, λαθὼν τοὺς ἐπορμέοντας having escaped the blockading fleet, Hdt.; ἐφ. τῷ λιμένι Thuc. 2. generally, to lie by and watch, Soph., Dem.

εφορμη.def: ἐφ-ορμή, ἡ, 1. a way of attack, μία δ’ οἴη γίγνετ’ ἐφορμή only room for one to attack, Od. 2. an assault, attack, Thuc.

εφορμησισ.gloss: a lying at anchor so as to watch
εφορμησισ.def: ἐφόρμησις, εως (ἐφορμέω) a lying at anchor so as to watch an enemy, blockading, Thuc.: a means of so doing, id.

εφορμιζω.def: ἐφορμίζω attic ιῶ I. to bring a ship to its moorings (ὅρμος): — Mid. and Pass. to come to anchor, Thuc. II. intr. in Act. to seek refuge in a place, c. dat., Anth.

εφοροσ.def: ἔφορος, ὁ, (ἐφοράω) I. an overseer, guardian, ruler, Aesch., Soph. II. at Sparta, ἔφοροι, οἱ, the Ephors, a body of five magistrates, who controlled even the kings, Hdt., etc.

εφυβριζω.def: ἐφυβρίζω fut. σω I. to insult over one, Il.; c. dat., Soph.; c. acc., in Mid., μὴ ’φυβρίζεσθαι νεκρούς Eur.; ἐφύβριζον ἄλλα τε καὶ εἰ they used insulting language, asking especially whether, Thuc. II. to exult maliciously over, Soph.

εφυδριασ.def: ἐφυδριάς, άδος, of the water, Νύμφη Anth. (from ἔφυδρος)

εφυδροσ.def: ἔφυδρος (ὕδωρ) 1. wet, moist, rainy, of the west wind, Od. 2. well-watered, Hdt.

εφυμνεω.def: ἐφυμνέω fut. ήσω I. to sing or chant after or over, τί τινι Aesch., Soph. II. to sing a dirge besides, Soph. III. to sing of, descant on, c. acc., id.

εφυπερθε.def: ἐφύπερθε above, atop, above, Hom.:— from above, Od.:—c. gen., Theocr.

εφυρα.def: Ἐφύρα Ephyra, old name of Corinth, Il.

εφυστεριζω.def: ἐφυστερίζω fut. σω to come later, τὰ ἐφυστερίζοντα αἱ ὑστεροῦσαι πόλεις, Thuc.

εφυω.def: ἐφύω to rain upon:—perf. pass. part. ἐφυσμένος rained upon, exposed to the rain, Xen.

εχεγγυοσ.def: ἐχ-έγγυος, ον (ἐγγύη) I. having given or able to give security, trust-worthy, secure, Eur.; ζημία ἐχ. a penalty to be relied on (for the prevention of crime), Thuc.: τὸ ἐχέγγυον security, Hdt.: c. inf. sufficiently strong to do, Plut. II. pass. having received a pledge, secured against danger, Soph.

εχεθυμοσ.def: ἐχέ-θῡμος, ον master of one's passion, Od.

εχεμυθεω.def: ἐχεμυθέω fut. ήσω to hold one's peace, Luc. (from ἐχέμῡθος)

εχεμυθια.def: ἐχεμῡθία, ἡ, silence, reserve, Plut. (from ἐχέμῡθος)

εχεπευκησ.def: ἐχε-πευκής, ές (πεύκη) Homeric epith. of a dart, bitter, or rather sharp-pointed, piercing, Il.

εχετησ.def: ἐχέτης, ου, = ὁ ἔχων, a man of substance, Pind.

εχετλη.def: ἐχέτλη, ἡ, (ἔχω) a plough-handle, Lat. stiva, Hes.

εχετληεισ.def: ἐχετλήεις, εσσα, εν of or belonging to a ploughhandle, Anth.

εχεφρονεω.def: ἐχεφρονέω to be prudent, Anth. (from ἐχέφρων)

εχεφροσυνη.def: ἐχεφροσύνη, ἡ, prudence, good sense, Anth. (from ἐχέφρων)

εχεφρων.def: ἐχέ-φρων, ονος, (φρήν) sensible, prudent, discreet, Hom.

εχθαιρω.def: ἐχθαίρω (ἔχθος) to hate, detest, Hom., Trag.; c. acc. cogn., ἔχθος ἐχθήρας μέγα hating with great hatred, Soph.:—Pass. to be hated, hateful, Trag.; so in fut. mid., ἐχθαρεῖ μὲν ἐξ ἐμοῦ Soph.

εχθαρτεοσ.def: ἐχθαρτέος, η, ον (verb. adj.) to be hated, Soph.

εχθεσ.def: ἐχθές (v. χθές) yesterday, Ar.; ἀπ’ ἐχθές Anth.; νῦν τε κἀχθές to-day or yesterday, Soph.; cf. πρώην.

εχθεσινοσ.def: ἐχθεσῐνός, ή, όν (= χθεσινός) yesterday's, Anth.

εχθιστοσ.def: ἔχθιστος, η, ον irreg. Sup. of ἐχθρός 1. most hated, most hateful, Il., Trag. 2. most hostile, Thuc.; c. gen., as if a Subst., οἱ ἐκείνου ἔχθ. his bitterest enemies, Xen.

εχθιων.def: ἐχθίων, ονος, more hated, more hateful, Trag. adv., ἐχθιόνως ἔχειν to be more hostile, Xen. (irreg. comp. of ἐχθρός,)

εχθοδοπεω.def: ἐχθοδοπέω fut. ήσω in hostility with another, c. dat., Il.

εχθοδοποσ.def: ἐχθοδοπός, όν (lengthd. form of ἐχθρός,) hateful, detestable, Soph., Ar., Plat.

εχθοσ.def: ἔχθος, εος, I. hate, hatred, Hom., etc.; ἔχθος τινός hatred for one, Hdt., Thuc.; ἐς ἔχθος ἀπικέσθαι τινί to incur his hatred or enmity, Hdt.; εἰς ἔχθος ἐλθεῖν τινί Eur. II. of persons, ὦ πλεῖστον ἔχθος object of direst hate, Aesch.

εχθραινω.def: ἐχθραίνω (ἐχθρός) (later form of ἐχθαίρω) to hate, Xen., Plut.

εχθρη.def: ἔχθρη, ἡ, (ἐχθρός) hatred, enmity, Hdt., attic; ἔχθρα τινός hatred for, enmity to one, Thuc.; κατ’ ἔχθραν τινός Ar.; ἔχθρα ἔς τινα Hdt.; ἔχθρα πρός τινα Aesch.; δι’ ἔχθρας ἀφικέσθαι, ἐλθεῖν τινί to be at feud with one, Eur., etc.; ἔχθραν συμβάλλειν, συνάπτειν τινί to engage in hostility with.., id.; ἔχθραν λύειν, διαλύεσθαι id., Thuc.

εχθροδαιμων.def: ἐχθροδαίμων hated of the gods, Soph.

εχθροξενοσ.def: ἐχθρό-ξενος, ον hostile to guests, inhospitable, Aesch., Eur.

εχθροσ.def: ἐχθρός, ή, όν (ἔχθος) I. hated, hateful, Hom., etc.; ἐχθρόν μοί ἐστιν, c. inf., 'tis hateful to me to.., Il. II. act. hostile, at enmity with, τινι Thuc., etc. III. as Subst., ἐχθρός, ὁ, one's enemy, Hes., etc.; ὁ Διὸς ἐχθρός Aesch.; οἱ ἐμοὶ ἐχθροί Thuc. IV. the regul. comp. and Sup. ἐχθρότερος, -τατος are rare: the irreg. ἐχθίων, ἔχθιστος being more used. V. adv. ἐχθρῶς, Plat., etc.; comp. ἐχθροτέρως, Dem.

εχθω.def: ἔχθω (ἔχθος) to hate, Soph., Eur.:—Pass. to be hated, detested, Hom., Aesch.

εχιδνα.def: ἔχιδνα, ἡ, (ἔχις) an adder, viper, Hdt., Trag., etc.; metaph. of a treacherous wife or friend, Aesch., Soph.

εχιδναιοσ.def: ἐχιδναῖος, η, ον of or like a viper, Anth.

εχιναι.gloss: the islands in the Ionian sea
εχιναι.def: Ἐχῖναι the islands in the Ionian sea, Il., Eur., etc.; commonly called Ἐχινάδες.

εχινεεσ.gloss: a kind of mouse with bristly hair
εχινεεσ.def: ἐχινέες a kind of mouse with bristly hair, in Libya, Hdt.

εχινοσ.def: ἐχῖνος I. the urchin, hedgehog, Ar., etc. 2. the sea-urchin, Plat. II. the shell of the sea-urchin, often used as a cup: then like Lat. testa, a pot, jug, pitcher, Lat. echinus, Ar., etc.:— the vase in which the notes of evidence were deposited, Dem. III. in pl. sharp points at each end of a bit, Xen.

εχισ.def: ἔχις an adder, viper, Plat.; metaph., συκοφάντης καὶ ἔχις τὴν φύσιν Dem.

εχμα.def: ἔχμα, ατος, τό, (ἔχω) that which holds; and so, I. a hindrance, obstacle, Il. 2. c. gen. a bulwark, defence against a thing, c. gen., Hhymn. II. a hold-fast, stay, ἔχματα πέτρης bands of rock, Il.; ἔχματα πύργων stays of the towers, id.; ἔχματα νηῶν props for the ships, to keep them upright, id.

εχυροσ.def: ἐχῠρός, ή, όν (ἔχω) I. strong, secure, of Places, Thuc., etc.; ἐν ἐχυρῷ εἶναι to be in safety, id.; ἐν ἐχυρωτάτῳ ποιεῖσθαί τι Xen. 2. of reasons, etc., trustworthy, Thuc. II. adv. -ρῶς, id.; comp. -ώτερον, id.

εχω.def: ἔχω (for the poet. form ἔσχεθον v. ⁎σχέθω) (the aor2 mid. is also used in pass. sense.) A. Trans., in two senses, to have or to hold: I. to have, possess, Hom., etc.; ὁ ἔχων a wealthy man, Soph.; οἱ οὐκ ἔχοντες the poor, Eur.:—c. gen. partit., μαντικῆς ἔχ. τέχνης Soph.:—Pass. to be possessed by, belong to, τινι Il. 2. to have charge of, keep, πύλας id.; φυλακὰς ἔχον kept watch, id., etc. 3. c. acc. loci, to dwell in, inhabit, haunt, Hom., etc. 4. to have to wife, id., etc. 5. to have in one's house, to entertain, Od. 6. the pres. part. is joined with a Verb, ἔχων ἀτίταλλε kept and made much of, i. e. kept with special care, Il.; ὃς ἂν ἥκηι ἔχων στρατόν whoever may have come with an army, Hdt. 7. of Habits or Conditions, γῆρας ἔχ., periphr. for γηράσκειν, Od. 8. like Lat. teneo, to know, understand, Il., Aesch.; ἔχεις τι; tenes? d' ye understand? Ar. 9. to involve, imply, give cause for, ἀγανάκτησιν Thuc. 10. ἔχειν σταθμόν to weigh so much, Hdt. II. to hold, Hom., etc.; ἔχ. ἐν χερσίν Hdt.; μετὰ χερσίν Il.; διὰ χειρός Soph., etc. 2. to hold fast, ἔχειν τινὰ χειρός, ποδός to hold him by the hand, by the foot, Il.; ἔχειν τινὰ μέσον to grip one by the middle, of wrestlers, Ar. 3. of a woman, to be pregnant, Lat. utero gestare, Hdt.; ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχειν id. 4. to hold out, bear up against, support, sustain an attack, Lat. sustinere; in which sense Hom. uses fut. σχήσω, σχήσομαι. 5. to hold fast, keep close, as bars do a gate, Il.: to enclose, Hom. 6. to hold or keep in a certain direction, like ἐπέχω, ὀϊστὸν ἔχε he aimed it, Il.; of horses or ships, to guide, drive, steer, id.; then absol., τῆι ῥ’ ἔχε that way he held his course, id.:—also to put in, land, εἰς or πρὸς τόπον Hdt.; δεῦρο νοῦν ἔχε attend to this, Eur.; πρός τι τὸν νοῦν ἔχ. Thuc. 7. to hold in, stay, keep back, ἵππους Il., etc.; οὐ σχήσει χεῖρας will not withhold his hands, Od.; ὀδύνας ἔχ. to allay, assuage them, Il., etc. 8. to keep away from, c. gen. rei, τινὰ ἀγοράων, νεῶν id.:—in attic to stop or hinder from doing, τοῦ μὴ καταδῦναι Xen.; ἔσχον μὴ κατανεῖν Eur. 9. to keep back, withhold a thing, χρήματα Od., etc. 10. to hold in guard, keep safe, protect, Il. III. c. inf. to have means or power to do, to be able, c. inf., Hom., etc.:—with inf. omitted, οὔπως εἶχε he could not, Il. 2. after Hom., οὐκ ἔχω ὅπως I know not how, etc., Soph., etc.; οὐκ ἔχω ὅ τι χρὴ λέγειν Xen. B. intr. to hold oneself, to keep so and so, ἕξω, ὡς ὅτε τις λίθος.. I will hold fast, as a stone.., Od.; σχὲς οὗπερ εἶ keep where thou art, Soph.; ἔχειν κατὰ χώραν to keep in one's place, Ar., etc.; διὰ φυλακῆς ἔχειν to keep on one's guard, Thuc. 2. c. gen. to keep from, πολέμου id. 3. c. gen., also, to take part in, have to do with, τέχνης Soph.: to be engaged or busy, ἀμφί τι Aesch.; περί τι Xen. II. simply to be, often with Advs. of manner, εὖ ἔχει Od.; καλῶς ἔχει, κακῶς ἔχει, Lat. bene habet, male habet, it is going on well, attic; οὕτως ἔχει so the case stands, Ar., etc.:—a gen. modi is often added, εὖ ἔχειν τινός to be well off for a thing, abound in it, Hdt.; ὡς ποδῶν εἶχον as fast as they could go, id.; ὥς τις εὐνοίας ἢ μνήμης ἔχοι as each man felt disposed or remembered, Thuc. III. to lead towards, ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμόν Hdt.; ἔχ. εἴς τι, to point towards, tend towards, id.; τὸ ἐς Ἀργείους ἔχον what concerns them, id.; also, ἔπ’ ὅσον ἔποψις εἶχε so far as the view extended, id. 2. ἐπί τινι ἔχειν to have hostile feelings towards.., id., Soph. IV. after Hom., ἔχω is joined with aor. part. of another Verb, κρύψαντες ἔχουσι for κεκρύφασι, Hes.; ἀποκληΐσας ἔχεις for ἀποκέκλεικας, Hdt.;—sometimes it gives a pres. sense to the aor., as, θαυμάσας ἔχω I am in a state of wonderment, Soph.; ὅς σφε νῦν ἀτιμάσας ἔχει who now treats her with dishonour, Eur. 2. the part. ἔχων, with the pres., adds a notion of duration, as, τί κυπτάζεις ἔχων; why do you keep poking about there? Ar.; φλυαρεῖς, ληρεῖς ἔχων you keep chattering, trifling, Plat. 3. pleonast., ἐστὶν ἔχον ἔχει, Hdt.; εστὶν ἀναγκαίως ἔχον ἔχει ἀναγκαίως, Aesch. C. Mid. to hold on by, cling to, c. gen., Hom., etc. 2. metaph. to cleave or cling to, ἔργου Hdt.; ἐλπίδος Eur.; τῆς αὐτῆς γνώμης Thuc.: to lay claim to a thing, Hdt.; to be zealous for, μάχης Soph. 3. to come next to, follow closely, Xen.; τῆς πληγῆς ἔχεται follows up the blow, Dem.:—of peoples or places, to be close, touch, border on, τινος Hdt., etc.; οἱ ἐχόμενοι the neighbouring people, id.: of Time, τὸ ἐχόμενον ἔτος the next year, Thuc. 4. to depend on, τινος or ἔκ τινος Hom. 5. to pertain to, τινος Hdt. II. to bear or hold for oneself, Hom. III. to maintain oneself, hold one's ground, Il. 2. c. acc. to keep off from oneself, repel, id. IV. to stop oneself, stop, id.:— to keep oneself back, abstain or refrain from, Hom., etc.

εψανδρα.def: ἑψ-άνδρα, ἡ, (ἀνήρ) cooking men, of Medea, Anth.

εψημα.def: ἕψημα, ατος, τό, anything boiled: pl. vegetables for kitchen use, Plat.

εψητηρ.def: ἑψητήρ (ἕψω) a pan for boiling, Anth.

εψητοσ.def: ἑψητός (ἕψω) boiled, Xen.: ἑψητοί, ῶν, οἱ, boiled fish, Ar.

εψια.def: ἑψία, ἡ, a game played with pebbles.

εψιαομαι.def: ἑψιάομαι (from ἑψία) Dep. to play with pebbles, generally, to amuse oneself, ἑψιαάσθων (epic 3rd dual imperat.), Od.; ἑψιάασθαι μολπῇ καὶ φόρμιγγι (epic inf.) id.

εψιλον.def: ἔψιλον Ε, ε, fifth letter of the Gr. alphabet: as numeral εʹ = πέντε and πέμπτος, but ͵ε = 5000. The ancients called this vowel εἶ (as they called ο, οὖ). When in the archonship of Euclides (B. C. 403) the Athenians adopted long e (Η η) from the Samian alphabet, the Gramm. gave to short e the name of ἒ ψιλόν, i. e. ε without the aspirate, because Ε had been used for the aspirate. In ionic, ε sometimes stood for ᾰ, βέρεθρον ἔρσην τέσσερες for βάραθρον ἄρσην τέσσαρες, and in contr. Verbs in -άω, as ὁρέω φοιτέω.

εψω.def: ἕψω 1. to boil, seethe, Hdt., attic: proverb. of useless labour, λίθον ἕψεις Ar.; c. gen. partit., ἥψομεν τοῦ κορκόρου we boiled some pimpernel, id.:—Pass. to be boiled, Hdt. 2. of metals, to smelt, refine, Pind. 3. metaph., γῆρας ἀνώνυμον ἕψειν to cherish an inglorious age, id.

εωθεν.def: ἕωθεν 1. from morn, i. e. at earliest dawn, early in the morning, Plat.; ἕ. εὐθύς Ar. 2. αὔριον ἕ. to-morrow early, Xen.; so ἕωθεν alone, Ar.

εωθινοσ.def: ἑωθῐνός, ή, όν (ἕως) in the morning, early, Hdt., Ar.: —τὸ ἑωθινόν, as adv., early in the morning, Hdt.; so, ἐξ ἑωθινοῦ ἕωθεν, Xen.

εωλοκρασια.gloss: a mixture of the dregs and heel-taps
εωλοκρασια.def: ἑωλοκρασία (κρᾶσις) a mixture of the dregs and heel-taps, with which the drunken were dosed at the end of a revel; metaph., ἑωλοκρασίαν μου τῆς πονηρίας κατασκεδάσας having discharged the stale dregs of his rascality over me, Dem.

εωλοσ.gloss: a day old, kept till the morrow, stale
εωλοσ.def: ἕωλος, ον (prob. from ἕως, ἠώς) 1. a day old, kept till the morrow, stale, Comici; ἕωλος θρυαλλίς a stinking wick (after the lamp has been blown out), Luc. 2. of actions or events, stale, out of date, Dem. 3. of men, coming a day too late, Plut.

εωμεν.def: ἑῶμεν ἐπεί χ’ ἑῶμεν πολέμοιο when we have enough of war:—but prob. it should be written
ἔωμεν (1st pl. subj. of ἄω, II.) to take one's fill of a thing.

εωοσ.def: ἑῷος, η, ον (ἕως) 1. in or of the morning, at morn, early, πάχνη ἑῴα the morning rime, Aesch.; ἑῷος ἐξαναστῆναι to get up early, Eur. 2. eastern, Xen.

εωρα.def: ἐώρα, ἡ, collat. form of αἰώρα, a halter, Soph.

εωσ.def: ἕως I. until, till, Lat. donec, dum, Hom.:—in Hom. sometimes used = τέως, for a time:—to express a fact, ἕως is foll. by Ind., εἷος φίλον ὤλεσε θυμόν Il.; when the event is uncertain, by the opt., ἕως ὅ γε μιγείη till he should reach, Od. b. ἕως ἄν or κε with Subj., relating to an uncertain event in future time, μαχήσομαι, εἵως κε κιχείω till I find, Il. 2. while, so long as, εἵως πολεμίζομεν Od.; ἕως ἔτι ἐλπίς [ἦν] Thuc. II. as adv., Lat. usque, mostly with Advs. of Time, ἕως ὅτε, Lat. usque dum, till the time when, Xen.; so, ἕως οὗ Hdt.; ἕως ὀψέ till late, Thuc.:—c. gen., ἕως τοῦ ἀποτῖσαι till he made payment, ap. Aeschin.

εωσπερ.def: ἕωσπερ (strengthd. for ἕως,) even until, Thuc.

εωσφοροσ.def: Ἑωσφόρος bringer of morn, Lat. Lucifer, the Morning-star.
